On or before October 24th, three herders (out of a group of seven) were killed and another injured when bandits fired upon them. The herders were making their way from Kapoa to Ameyan market (coordinates for Kapedo, Barringo, used).
On or before October 24th, demonstrators gathered in Machakos to protest against the poor condition of a road connecting Katangi to Matuu, and for the failure of local authorities to pave the road.

On or before October 24th, teachers gathered in Litein (Kericho) to protest the killing of a colleague in July, and specifically the lack of police response to the murder. The source mentions that the 'demonstration turned violent as police dispersed the teachers from the streets' (the demonstrators have been coded as protesters rather than rioters, since it is not specified whether they engaged in violent activity).
'A male staff member of an INGO was attacked by unknown assailants near his residence during the evening. The attack led to severe head injuries and a crack on his skull.'
On or before October 22nd, teachers gathered in Mbita (Homa Bay) to protest the murder of a colleague on October 13th, and the failure of police to arrest any suspects.

On 19 October 2018, police clashed with an armed gang in Kayole (Nairobi). One gang member was killed, and a police officer is in critical condition after being shot in the head. Police were reported to have arrested 200 local residents, which the source described as 'suspects'.
October 19th (on or before) police arrested 200 local residents described as 'suspects' after an earlier clash with gang members in Kayole.

On or before October 17th, two people were killed in a clash in Jaldesa (Marsabit), and two police reservists were wounded in the crossfire. The violence comes amidst recent ethnically-motivated clashes in the area. A number of local politicians have been questioned.

During the week beginning October 15th, clashes occurred at an unspecified location in Marsabit amidst ethnic violence. 10 killed (coded as 8 here and 2 for a clash in Jaldesa). Two local politicians were arrested on October 22nd over their alleged role in the violence.

On 17 October 2018, students protested at the University of Machakos (Machakos), over a stipulation that they return to the University with their parents. The University closed indefinitely three weeks prior after student protests over an increase in fees. One person was arrested and later released.

On 16 October 2018, police arrested 40 people (including a local politician) over the invasion of a 900-acre Agricultural Development Corporation (ADC) land in Kisiwani, Kilifi County. The arrests took place in Kwa Ndomo in Sabaki ward.

On 16 October 2018, police fired their weapons into the air to scatter a crowd of protesters in Kisiwani (Kilifi). This followed the arrest of 40 people (including a local politician) for invading an area of disputed land.

On 16 October 2018, Al Shabaab militants alleged that they had destroyed two Kenyan military vehicles with an IED, killing and injuring an unspecified number of soldiers. The alleged incident took place between Fino and Arabiya villages in Mandera county (coordinates for Fino, Mandera, used). Subsequent reports indicate that the IED exploded before the military vehicles were in range, resulting in no casualties or fatalities.
On 12 October 2018, two robbery suspects were lynched by a mob in Kiptule area of Kericho West subcounty. The suspects were stoned to death after confessing their criminal activities.

On 12 October 2018, students from the Mombasa branch of the University of Nairobi protested the killing of a UoN student and another man by a mob on 7 Oct. The student was lynched in an alleged case of mistaken identity.

On 12 October 2018, a British-South African manager of the Olarro Nature Conservancy was shot in the head with an arrow at close range in Maji Moto (Narok). The attacker was wearing Maasai clothing. The manager fired two shots in the air, before escaping. He was patrolling near a disputed dam, that Maji Moto communities accused the conservationists of badly managing.

On 12 October 2018, an armed group attacked Shurr village in Marsabit county (coordinates for the state capital of Marsabit town used). In the ensuing gunfight, three residents of the town were killed, as was one of the attackers. The source describes the clash as being 'ethnic' in nature.
On 11 October 2018, residents of Jumba Ruins in Mtwapa, Mombasa county held a protest in the locality over the alleged grabbing of a 127-acre land they claim to own.

On 11 October 2018, bandits raided the village of Chemisto in Sigor constituency (coordinates for Sigor, West Pokot, used). They killed two civilian, including a child. The bandits also stole a significant amount of livestock. The attack comes three day after a truce was signed between the Pokot and Marakwet, which had been intended to put an end to such raiding and reprisal attacks.

On 11 October 2018, hundreds of South Sudanese residents in Kenya and Kenyans protested in Nairobi against the political and military elite of South Sudan, and the alleged complicity of individuals and economic institutions in Kenya in the process of such accumulation.They called upon the Kenyan government to seize wealth and assets that South Sudanese elites had stored in the Kenyan banking system.

On 10 October 2018, around twenty militants suspected to belong to Al Shabaab attacked a school in Lafey (Mandera). The militants targeted non-Muslim staff, and threw an explosive device into quarters used by non-Muslim teachers, killing two.
On or before October 9th, the residents of Tunen in Trans Nzoia (approximate coordinates used closed to the border with Uasin) protested against land grabbing in the area.

On 9 October 2018, an armed group (described as bandits in the source) attacked the village of Nkiruni in Tharaka-North county (coordinates for county capital of Kathwana used). The group abducted a mother and her two daughters, and released two soon after. They also looted livestock from the area.
On 9 October 2018, a mob set ablaze a motorcycle in Thika (Thika Town, Kiambu), whose owner had allegedly attempted to snatch a woman's handbag. The owner managed to escape.

notes: On 9 October 2018, prison guards pursuing an escaped convict attacked 'dozens' of residents of a deprived neighbourhood in Nyeri. A prison official said that no reports of abuse had been filed.
On 9 October 2018, a mob set ablaze a motorcycle in Nairobi (Starehe, Nairobi), whose owner had allegedly attempted to snatch a woman's handbag. The owner managed to escape.

On or around October 8th, around 1,000 protesters from Maji Moto bloked the Narok-Sikinani road, over a variety of disputes between the community and the Olarro Nature Conservancy, including the shooting of cattle and access to water sources. The Maasai community accused the conservancy of failing to constitute a proper management plan, to conduct elections of officials and a conservancy committee, and to review the land lease agreement.
On 8 October 2018, a truce was signed between the Pokot and Marakwet to put an end to raiding and reprisal attacks.

On 8 October 2018, 35 families of the late senior chief Wambugu Mathangani demonstrated by locking the gates leading to the Wambugu agricultural training centre in Nyeri (Nyeri Central, Nyeri), against the forceful acquisition of their land by the government. The group demanded the government to compensate them for the loss of their land.

On 7 October 2018, a vigilante mob beat and set fire to two civilians who had been mistaken for thieves, as they left a drinking establishment in Mombassa. Both men (who were relatives) were killed in the attack.
On 6 October 2018, students gathered at the University of Kabianga (Kericho county) to protest against the killing of a fellow student, who had been found with stab wounds earlier that day.
On 5 October 2018, dozens of local residents staged a protest in Kutus town, Kirinyaga demanding the arrest of Josephine Kabura for lying in NYS affidavit.

On 5 October 2018, demonstrators barricaded roads in Gilgil town (Nakuru county), in protest at a spate of attacks and murders in the area. Riot police fired tear gas at the demonstrators, dispersing them.

On 2 October 2018, long distance truck drivers demonstrated by blocking the Malaba border (Teso North, Busia), against delays and alleged harassment by both customs and police officers. The group demanded to be involved as well as given able time before effecting any changes.
On 2 October 2018, around 2 000 workers from Karuturi Flower Farm demonstrated in Naivasha (Lake View, Naivasha, Nakuru) against Stanbic Bank failure in paying them their dues.

On 2 October 2018, during a violent demonstration at the county assembly at Homa Bay town (coded in a separate event), police assaulted a journalist from the Kenya Standard who was covering the demonstration.

On 2 October 2018, demonstrators broke into the county assembly at Homa Bay town amidst a political leadership dispute and threw stones at staff members. Police used tear gas to disperse the crowd. A journalist from the Kenya Standard who was covering the demonstration was assaulted by police during the event (coded in a separate event).
On or before October 2nd, Kenyan security services fired at civilians in Madera county (precise location unspecified). At least one person was injured.

Around 1 October 2018 (as reported), military officers beat up local residents, torched houses and burnt livestock in El Wak (Mandera South, Mandera), after an IED was found on Elwak Kutollow road. One person died while 17 others sustained injuries during the incident.

On 1 October 2018, 12 gang members broke into a biscuit factory in Thika town (Kiambu county), and assaulted the security guards, before looting goods from the factory. Police arrived and shot six of the robbers dead, whilst six of the robbers fled the scene, apparently after all had sustained gunshot wounds. The police claimed that one of the gang members was in possession of a crude firearm.

Around 29 September 2018 (as reported), a mob torched a vehicle belonging to a traffic officer in along Kangari road in Kangare [Kigumo, Muranga], for allegedly causing the death of a bodaboda taxi rider. Police used teargas to disperse the crowd from the scene.
On or before September 29th, protesters gathered at Jomvu (Mombasa) to demonstrate against land grabbing and the fraudlent sale of public land in the area.
27 September 2018: 2 people were reportedly killed by unidentified gunmen near Karasani town as they traveled to Lokori from Kapedo.

On 27 September 2018, local Turkana residents stopped and blocked (through unspecified means) five trucks transporting oil from Ngamia 8 to Mombasa along the Lokichar-Kitale Highway [coded as Lokichar, Turkana South, Turkana]. The group demanded that the trucks return to Africa Camp Solutions.

On 27 September 2018, matutu (minibus) drivers and local merchants protested the alleged failure of the police to investigate reports of Mungiki activity in Nairobi, who they have say have been extorting matatu operators, and were behind the recent murder of a matatu driver who refused to pay protection fees. Police denied the claims, saying they arrested several gang members.

27 September 2018: Following an IED landmine attack the day before, Kenyen security forces raided the Daba city village in Mandara county and beat local residents with clubs and kicking them. At least 22 unarmed civilians were hurt during the event.

On 26 September 2018, two children were killed near Nakuyen village, North Pokot after they touched and played with a RDX explosive device, which exploded. The device had been left in the area by the military who had conducted an operation locally.

From September 24th - 26th, students demonstrated against fee increases at the University of Machakos (Machokos). Police dispersed protesters with tear gas on Monday 24th; arrested a student leader on the 25th; and again dispersed protesters on the 26th (the source does not specify how). The University was indefinitely closed as of Sep 26th.
26 September 2018: An IED hit a Kenyan military vehicle in Daba-city village in Mandera County.

From September 24th - 26th, students demonstrated against fee increases at the University of Machakos (Machokos). Police dispersed protesters with tear gas on Monday 24th; arrested a student leader on the 25th; and again dispersed protesters on the 26th (the source does not specify how). The University was indefinitely closed as of Sep 26th.

On 25 September 2018, residents of Githurai town, Kiambu, staged road blocks and set up bonfires on Thika Superhighway in protest against the police's slow response to remove debris and bodies following a road accident in the area. Youth allegedly hurled stones at the police who arrived later and used tear gas to disperse them.

On 25 September 2018, a pro-Al Shabaab radio station reported that Al Shabaab forces had attacked a KDF camp at Taksile, north of Lamu (coordinates for Lamu used). According to the source, 10 KDF soldiers were killed, and three Al Shabaab fighters were also killed.

24 September 2018: Al-Shabaab militants claim to have overrun a Kenyan military base in Taksile area north of Pandaguo, Lamu County, killing 10 Kenyan soldiers and admitting three deaths among their own ranks. Kenyan military sources also reported the clashes, although they claimed that 10 Al-Shabaab fighters had been killed. Fatalities coded at the most conservative estimate.

On 24 September 2018, KDF soldiers attacked an Al Shabaab hideout at Taksile, north of Lamu (coordinates for Lamu used), killing 10 Al Shabaab fighters, and seizing weapons and ammunition. 3 KDF soldiers were reported to have been injured in the attack and weapons were recovered.

From September 24th - 26th, students demonstrated against fee increases at the University of Machakos (Machokos). Police dispersed protesters with tear gas on Monday 24th; arrested a student leader on the 25th; and again dispersed protesters on the 26th (the source does not specify how). The University was indefinitely closed as of Sep 26th.

On 23 September 2018, around 400 Maasai demonstrators protested against a planned eviction from farmland whose ownership is contested by members of the Maasai and Kikyu communities. The event occurred at Mai Mahiu

On 22 September 2018, local labourers of a Chinese company contracted to lay tarmac on Suguta-Maralal road staged a protest in front of Sino Hydro's office in Maralal town denouncing poor working conditions and non-payment of overtime.
21 September 2018: Armed men from Marakwet village reportedly raided the Ng'oron village, Tirioko Tiaty Sub-county. According to the report, three people were killed and several others injured.

On 21 September 2018, a herder militia (believed to be Somali in ethnicity) attacked Muthungwe village (coordinates for Mutitu, Kitui, used). The group killed a man and seriously injured his wife, using machetes to do so. The motive for the attack is not clear.

On 21 September 2018, a gang of five men ambushed three people as they returned to Koromangucha village from a party in a nearby village (coordinates for Kuria East, Migori, used). One person was killed, and two others were wounded before they escaped. The attackers used machetes; there was no clear motive for the attack.
Around 21 September 2018 (as reported), police shot dead a matutu (minibus) tout in Dandora (Embakasi North, Nairobi), for allegedly smoking bhang.

On 21 September 2018, demonstrators - comprising youth and matutu operators - clashed with police in Dandora (Nariobi), with police using tear gas to scatter the protesters. The demonstrations were related to the shooting of a matutu tout by police.

On 21 September 2018, residents lit bonfires on major access roads, and waved placards in Dandora (Embakasi North, Nairobi), in a demonstration against harassment by police and haphazard shooting, following the killing of a matatu tout (coded separately).

On 20 September 2018, a suspected bandit shot dead two herders and a child in Kerio Valley or nearby area as a revenge for the family failing to share cows stolen by one of the victims and the perpetrator during a raid in Tiaty, Baringo county. The attacker later surrendered to the police.

19 September 2018: The Mombasa/Nairobi highway was blocked by protesting Matatu drivers from Mikindani to the Central Business District, Jomvu, Mombasa. The drivers protested the lack of parking space within the city. At least one person was arrested. The protests come as the Mikindani stage was shut down the night before by police officers armed with batons and tear gas.

On September 18th and 19th, a criminal gang attacked Ragumo and Ofunyu villages in Kisumu East constituency (coordinates for Nyamasaria, Kisumu used). The group assaulted an unspecified number of residents, and engaged in multiple counts of theft.

On 19 September 2018, around 1,000 workers at the Mumias Sugar Company (Kakamega) blockaded roads around the factory, in protest at the non-payment of salaries for 17 months, and alleged mismanagement at the firm.
On 19 September 2018, the police allegedly shot dead three youth in Dandora who were reportedly smoking marihuana (bhang).
On 18 September 2018, residents from Mitahato village in Githunguri blocked the Kirigiti-Kwamaiko road in protest over poor workmanship carried out on the road by the contractor.

On 18 September 2018, activists demonstrated in Meru town demanding justice for Githongo law court magistrate's daughter who had been abducted and killed. The protesters also demanded an overhaul of local police units and better security.

On September 18th and 19th, a criminal gang attacked Ragumo and Ofunyu villages in Kisumu East constituency (coordinates for Nyamasaria, Kisumu used). The group assaulted an unspecified number of residents, and engaged in multiple counts of theft.

On or around September 18th, an unidentified group carrying axes and machetes attacked and robbed the uncle of a murder victim, which is connected to the Governor of Migori county. The event happened in Nairobi, and the victim was able to fend off the attackers.
On 17 September 2018, a bread vendor was shot dead by the police near an armory at the AP line in Kigumo.

On 17 September 2018, a mob set a blaze two vehicles belonging to an lawyer in Kathangachwe (Tharaka, Tharaka-Nithi), over an alleged land dispute. Police officers fired in the air to disperse the mob and one person was injured during the incident.

On 17 September 2018, protesters from the Jubilee Party marched in Nakuru, in the hope of changing the county-level leadership of the party. The protesters attempted to storm the HQ of the county branch of the party, but were unable to gain access to the premises, which was reported to be deserted.
On 16 September 2018, the perpetrator of a fatal stabbing of a local teacher was beaten to death by a crowd at the outskits of Limuru town.
On 16 September 2018, 'heavily-armed' Ugandan police deployed to the disputed island of Migingo, prompting Kenyan fishermen to avoid sailing near the island.

Around 16 September 2018 (as reported), unidentified individuals killed a nine-year-old schoolgirl and daughter to a magistrate in Meru (Imenti North, Meru). The girl had been abducted on 6 September (coded separately).

On 15 September 2018, suspected Pokot militiamen shot and wounded three police officers in an ambush in Ramacha, Baringo South.
At an unspecified time (likely on or after mid-September, precision 3 used) the Mungiki sect reportedly murdered a matatu (minibus) operator in Nairobi, after he refused to pay them protection money.
On 14 September 2018, eight Al Shabaab gunmen ambushed a bus near Ijara, heading to Garissa. They profiled people travelling on the bus and killed two non-local passengers.

13 September 2018: Police forces opened fire at rioters throwing rocks at police officers in the town of El Wak, killing at least one person. On 13 September 2018, a mob accosted and lynched a suspected political militiaman whose group had been accused of causing mayhem in Junda area, Kisauni, Mombasa.

On 13 September 2018, further clashes were reported between the Ogiek and Kipsigi groups in Nessuit, Eastern Mau Forest (Nakuru, coordinates for Mau Narok used). One person was killed, and more houses were torched.

On 13 September 2018, a police officer fatally assaulted a minibus driver with his rifle. A mob formed and chased the police officer, lynching him. Another man (a boda boda driver) was killed in the violence. The events took place in the area of Kenyenya (Kisii), and a police Internal Affairs Unit has been dispatched to investigate.

13 September 2018: Police forces opened fire at rioters throwing rocks at police officers in the town of El Wak, killing at least one person. Rioters then entered the hospital compound and attacked non-locals, killing two and seriously injuring a third. They were demonstrating against the death of three people who they said were killed by security officers a day before. Coded as two separate events, one riot and one VAC event.
On 13 September 2018, armed men attacked and killed a Nyumba Kumi official, an unarmed community watch officer associated with police, at Barsheba area in Kisauni, Mombasa.

On 12 September 2018, informal traders staged a demonstration along Diani Beach Road in Kwale, protesting the ongoing demolition of their stalls ordered by the county government.

On 12 September 2018, two men were killed in Kilolapwa and Shamu villages in the area of Ukunda (Kwale county). On September 11th and 12th, armed clashes were reported in the Nessuiet, Mariashoni, Mauche, and other wards of Njoro county (Nakuru) between the Ogiek and Kipsigi groups, which resulted in 6 deaths (coded across 6 events) and 17 injuries. Houses were also torched in the clashes. The identities of the victims are not known. The clashes are likely spillover from violence in neighbouring Narok that flared up after a dispute over livestock theft and occupation of land on the edges of the Mau Forest.

On 12 September 2018, police killed two suspected gang members who had been active in the Juja area, at Karuguru close to the Eastern Bypass (coordinates for Juja, Kiambu, used). Eight gang members escaped.

12 September 2018: Security forces reportedly arrested a family of 5 in the town of El-Wak. Three of those arrested were later found dead, and local civilians have accused security forces of being responsible for their deaths.

During the week beginning September 10th, police shot dead three young men working on a dumpsite in Dandora (Nairobi). The police claimed one of the individuals was a notorious gangster, and that the deceased had been armed. The events have been contested by the family of one of the victims, who said that he worked at the dumpsite, and was not a robber.

On September 11th and 12th, armed clashes were reported in the Nessuiet, Mariashoni, Mauche, and other wards of Njoro county (Nakuru) between the Ogiek and Kipsigi groups, which resulted in 6 deaths (coded across 6 events) and 17 injuries. Houses were also torched in the clashes. The identities of the victims are not known. On 11 September 2018, a police vehicle belonging to the Anti-Stock Theft Unit was hit by an explosion in Kotulo ward (Wajir). They began searching for suspects afterwards. There were no reports of police injuries or deaths.

On 11 September 2018, police apprehended four members of the same family at Qababa village in Elram (Kotulo ward, Wajir). One was beaten before being released, and the other three were found dead the following day. All had been shot in the head. The police were conducting a search operation in the area following an attack on a police vehicle the same day.

On 11 September 2018, activists staged a protest in Nairobi against the murder of a Rongo University student who had been abducted together with the journalist Barrack Oduor. The protesters called on politicians to act upon the recent killing.

On 10 September 2018, matatu (minibus) operators blocked traffic on Murang'a - Kiriaini road in protest against the roads' dilapidated state. They demanded the road be re-carpeted instead of the government only investing in filling potholes.

On 10 September 2018, a 13 year old boy was hacked to death, and his 12 year old sister and 70 year old grandmother were wounded in the attack in Esimenwa village (coordinates for Narok town used). The attack follows violence between the Maasai and Kipsigi groups in the area the following week (which some reports attribute to conflicts over land titles, some to cattle rustling, and others to actions by the government and/or assorted local politicians), though the specific identity of the group of attackers is not specified in the source, nor is the ethnicity of the victims. Police have been deployed to the area, and a suspect has been arrested.

On 10 September 2018, the police allegedly shot dead a young man in Mtongwe, Mombasa following a raid in his home. The killing was done reportedly as part of the police's manhunt for a gang that has been attacking civilians in the local area.

Arrests: During the week leading up to 8th September, Kenyan police reportedly arrested 163 Pakistani nationals in the city of Mombasa, as part of a nation-wide crackdown on illegal immigration. On September 5th, police also raided the offices of the China Global Television Network in Nairobi, arresting 13 Chinese civilians (including journalists).
On or around 7 Sept 2018, tribal clashes erupted in Marsabit county following the recent killing of two people near Maasai Mau forest in Narok county.

Around 7 September 2018 (as reported), Maasai and Kipsigis militia armed with spears and bows and arrows clashed with each other in Olmekenyu (Narok South, Narok), following the recent killing of a herder, as well as land dispute and involvement of politicians. Two people were killed, 10 others wounded; and more than 60 houses torched during the incident.

On 6 September 2018, a man was shot with an arrow during a suspected revenge mission in Nkoben area near Maasai Mau forest in Narok county following the killing in the same area on 4 Sept. Tension in the community was high following the incidents.

On 6 September 2018, unidentified individuals abducted and killed a nine-year-old schoolgirl and daughter to a magistrate in Meru (Imenti North, Meru). Her body was later found on 16 September 2018 (coded separately).

notes: On 6 September 2018, police killed three youth who they said were suspected criminals at Utage (Mombasa county). Police dismissed claims that these were extra-judicial killings.

On 5 September 2018, two people were killed following armed clashes between Gabra and Borana pastoralist militia over pasture in Horonder, between Moyale and Marsabit. The first person died during clashes on 5 Sept, while the second passed away the following morning. Three other people were wounded.

On 4 September 2018, drivers were reported to have blocked roads in the area of Mt. Kenya (locations not specified, coordinates for Nyeri town used). This was in protest at the introduction of a (long-delayed) fuel tax.

On 4 September 2018, drivers were reported to have blocked part of the Kisii-Bomet highway (location not specified, coordinates for Bomet used). This was in protest at the introduction of a (long-delayed) fuel tax.

On 4 September 2018, a herder (of an unspecified ethnicity) was killed in the Nkoben area of the Maasai Mau forest (coordinates for Mau Narok used). This killing sparked two days of violence in Narok (see separate entries).

On or before September 4th, off-duty Kenyan police officers demanded bribes from civilians drinking at an illicit brewery in Sondu (Kericho). After detaining several civilians, a crowd formed to release them, and the police fired gunshots to disperse the crowd, wounding a bystander. Senior police are reported to be investigating the incident.

On or before September 4th, police killed three men suspected of murdering a local chief, in Kanyagia village (Nyeri county). Police activities against political militias have been stepped up in the area.

On or before September 3rd, armed gangsters raided a petrol station in Oyugis town (Homa Bay district). The two security guards at the station had their hands tied, and an unspecified amount of money was stolen. Two of the robbers were wearing police uniforms and carry AKs, whilst the remaining six were not.
On or before September 3rd, traders from the Maasai ethnic group demonstated against the demolition of their stalls in Uhuru market by authorities in Narok Town.

On or before September 3rd, Ugandan maritime police pursued Kenyan fisherman to Sumba island (Busia district), after they had allegedly been fishing in Ugandan waters. Upon reaching the island, Kenyan residents and fisherman threw stones at the Ugandan police, who fired shots in the air, before leaving. The residents of the island appealed to the Kenyan government to establish a police post on the island.

On 3 September 2018, a gang hired to evict a family (as part of a land dispute) were attacked by vigilantes, who killed one gang member. The incident took place at Kagumo-ini village (Muranga, coordinates for Kabati used).
On 3 September 2018, around 120 youth from Makueni county blocked the Machakos-Wote road in protests at unpaid wages for their work in upgrading work in the county (coordinates for Wote used).
On 3 September 2018, residents of Ngecha village (Kiambu county) demonstrated against a local gang known as the 'Gaza Boys'.

On 3 September 2018, a journalist and a pregnant University student were abducted in Migori. After being attacked, the journalist escaped the moving car he was in, sustaining serious injuries. The student's body was later found in a forest, having been stabbed multiple times, and likely raped. The personal assistant of Governor Okoth Obado has been arrested for allegdly orchestrating the kidnap and murder. Obado was himself charged with aiding and abetting the murder on September 24th.
On 3 September 2018, drivers of taxis, matatus and boda bodas barricaded roads in Nakuru town, in protest at the increase in fuel tax which came into effect that day.

On or before September 3rd, a militia comprising traders from the Maasai ethnic group attacked traders at Muthurwa market in Narok Town and set fire to the market, following the destruction of Maasai stalls by the local government. The Maasai were said to be armed, whilst the traders they were attacking used machetes to defend themselves. One person (from an unspecified group) was killed, and seven were injured. Police were also attacked once they became involved.

On 4 September 2018, around 1,000 residents of Kiambu (Mbeere South) marched to Gitaru power station in protest at the lack of adequate water availability (which they attributed to KenGen's dam-building activities). The protesters blockaded two roads in the area, damaged railings, and set fire to tires. Police prevented them from entering the power station itself.

On 30 August 2018, a group of activists held a peaceful protest in Mombasa over the disappearance of a local youth. They also raised concerns over the rising number of forced disappearances in the region.

On 30 August 2018, local clan members torched 14 houses in Kapyego, Marakwet East as an act of revenge towards the relatives of the man suspected to have shot dead an area acting chief. The chief had been shot dead by herders on suspicion he was a cattle thief.

On 29 August 2018, local residents demonstrated by waving placards and banners as they marched from Mukuyu to the governor's office in Muranga (Kiharu, Muranga), against the alleged governor interference in the management of water resources. The residents demanded the governor to stop interfering in the management of water resources.

On 28 August 2018, protestors barricaded the road between Emali and Wote (Makueni sub-county, coordinates for Emali used). The demonstrators were angry about the substandard condition of the road, and the failure of the three MPs of the region to address their concerns.

A mob lynched and burned three men in Siaya County on Tuesday on suspicion that they were part of a notorious gang in Siaya. The men were attacked at Malunga Village in West Gem.

On 16 January 2018, local residents, mainly youths protested by waving placards and shouting at the Liwatoni dumpsite in Ganjoni (Nyali, Mombasa), against a county directive confining the dumping of garbage to only 3 dump sites. The group demanded the county government address the garbage problem.

Evictions of local indigenous people led to the killing of a member of the local Sengwer community by Kenya Forest Service (KFS) rangers. Regarded as squatters by government, the Sengwer people have resisted efforts to move them from the Embobut Forest, which they see as ancestral lands.
Since December 2017, more than [8] people have been killed in clashes between members of the Arjuran and Degodia clans at the Eldas and Wajir North sub-counties boundary. Dates not provided.
Armed groups killed a woman and injured five police officers at Nyongoro along the Lamu-Malindi road

Around 15 January 2018 (as reported), local residents invaded a dweller house in Bungoma (Township, Kanduyi, Bungoma) as revenge after a murder. The dweller son was killed by the mob while his parents were seriously injured. Property was destroyed in the compound.
On 14 January 2018, unidentified group shot and killed one person in Kapedo (Tiaty, Baringo).
On 14 January 2018, suspected Pokot militia clashed with a group of four Samburu herders at Lomirok area of Baragoi (Samburu North, Samburu). One herder was injured during the incident.
Youngsters gathered to protest against the arrests of three people for Saturday's events.
People violently demonstrated against the arrest of a local sheikh and destroyed property, especially churches. Three dead.
Kenyan officials said a civilian was killed and several policemen wounded when suspected members of the Somalia-based group al-Shabaab attacked a convoy of vehicles.
On 12 January 2018, a woman was burnt to death while her husband was shot and injured when gunmen invaded their home in Nyamira County on Friday night.

On 11 January 2018, Kapenguria boys high school students demonstrated by marching to the office of the county director of education in Kapenguria (West Pokot, West Pokot), against the transfer of their head teacher. The school closed indefinitely.

On 11 January 2018, about 80 Kisukioni secondary school students demonstrated by marching to the office of the governor in Machakos (Machakos, Machakos), against the underperformance and mismanagement of the institution by the principal. The Police talked to the students and transported them back to school.

On 11 January 2018, a group, including students, demonstrated at the St. Joseph's girls school, Kibwezi (Kibwezi West, Makueni), against the transfer of the school principal. 6 people tried to stop current Principal from entering the school by surrounding her; Police intervened and arrested them.
On 10 January 2018, a mob lynched a man in Kiboore village near Kinangop (Kinangop, Nyandarua), for allegedly raping a girl.

One person has been shot dead in Bonyunyu, Nyamira County as villagers protested the planned construction of a controversial dam. Police also arrested three people among them two women even as villagers said they are not ready for the project.

Uneasy calm is slowly returning to St Mary's Mission Hospital in Gilgil, Nakuru County, after days of tension and violent confrontations due to a property ownership battle. The confrontations saw a vehicle torched and operations paralysed at the institution
Suspected al-Shabab militants have destroyed a Safaricom communication mast in Kutulo, Wajir County.
On 7 January 2018, private security guards beat up and injured a man at the Nyali centre (Nyali, Mombasa), for allegedly relieving himself at the centre. The victim later succumbed to the injuries.
Around 7 January 2018 (as reported), an unidentified armed group attacked Cheptulel (Lomut, Pokot Central, West Pokot). They killed four people and drove away with around 400 cattle.
Angry boda boda riders in Malindi on Saturday burnt down a Simba Coach bus after it hit and killed one of them along the Mombasa-Malindi highway
On 6 January 2018, suspected Pokot and Marakwet militias clashed at Tot (Marakwet East, Elgeyo Marakwet). Two people were killed, and several others sustained gunshot wounds.

On 6 January 2018, local residents blocked the Narok Mahi Mahiu road with stones and burning tires in Suswa (Kajiado west Kajiado), in demonstration against unfair employment by a company building the standard gauge railway (SGR). Police shot live bullets at the group. One person died during the incident.

More than 800 employees on Friday protested at the Satellite section in Mai Mahiu. Ongoing construction of the Nairobi-Naivasha phase of the Standard Gauge Railway (SGR) has been suspended in the last three days as workers protest low pay and harsh working conditions.
On 5 January 2018, suspected Marakwet militia attacked and killed three people in Koipogegh village near Chesogon (Pokot Central, West Pokot). The militia made away with over 300 heads of cattle.

On 5 January 2018, cattle rustlers attacked herders in Chesegon village near Tot (Endo, Marakwet East, Elgeyo Marakwet). They shot dead five people and made away stealing 300 cattle. Four people were seriously injured during the fight with police reservists.
A 32-year-old man was lynched by a mob after he killed his girlfriend following a domestic dispute in Kirindinyi Village, Voi in Taita Taveta County.

Al-Shabab has claimed responsibility for an attack on a Kenyan police station located along the common border in Mandera on 2 January. 'Reports from al-Shabab Mujahideen say that six soldiers (police) were killed in the attack with one being the commander of the police in the area, four were killed in the raid on the police camp while two other soldiers were killed in an ambush while they were rushing to back up their colleagues from El Waq town,' the website reported.

Al Shabaab terrorists have set on fire two police camps in Ijara, in the latest attack from the Somalia-based militant group. The attackers also destroyed the main communication equipment used in the town before speeding off with a police land cruiser which is yet to be recovered. A senior police officer briefed on the matter has told Capital News beat that no casualty was reported in the attack.

Transport along the busy Nairobi-Naivasha was Saturday morning paralysed for more than two hours after squatters at Soko Mjinga barricaded the road (Nairobi - Kibra) protesting a move to construct a high cost cemetery within the locality.

Commercial sex workers in Kisii Town on Friday protested against the killing of their colleague on Wednesday. They matched though Kisii Town streets, calling for justice, wearing red T-Shirts inscribed 'Stop Violence against Commercial Sex Workers'.

Schoolchildren were playing with a device when it exploded. At least five children have been killed in an explosion in Banisa, Mandera County. Banisa Sub-County Deputy County Commissioner Mathias Chisambo said the schoolchildren were playing with a grenade they had found in a grazing field.
Since December 2017, more than [8] people have been killed in clashes between members of the Arjuran and Degodia clans at the Eldas and Wajir North sub-counties boundary. Dates not provided.

Hundreds of non-locals in Lamu town took to the streets to protest against increased attacks and killings. The protests were precipitated by the killing of a 35-year-old man who was attacked with machetes and knives at Bombay area on Lamu Island on Saturday night.
Students are protesting against what they term as poor management at the institution. Daystar University was on Friday closed due to student unrest that has rocked the institution since November.

A suspected 'terrorist' was shot dead by police in Likoni area of Mombasa. According to area police Chief Benjamin Rotich, the suspect was cornered during a raid at his house at about 3 am. The report did not specify whether the man was armed.
Local villagers blockaded the UNHCR offices with burning barricades to protest against the Dadaab refugee camp.

Angry residents of Bahati in Nakuru County have stoned to death two armed gangsters who had stolen household items. Police boss Edward Masibo said that the armed robbers broke into the house of a man and stole items worth more than Sh200,000.
Local villagers blockaded the UNHCR offices with burning barricades to protest against the Dadaab refugee camp.

Two Administration Police officers have died while three others have been injured after suspected Al-Shabaab militants ambushed an escort vehicle they were travelling in at Lango La Simba in Nyongoro, along the Lamu-Malindi road.

Teargas fired at opposition leader Raila Odinga and his supporters as they attempted to rally in Nairobi. At least two people were shot dead in clashes with police. Odinga's supporters engaged in running battles with police as they attempted to gather for a 'memorial rally' to honour nearly 60 people killed, mostly by police, in over four months of political upheaval. Two people were shot dead in Soweto (in Nairobi) as police manned Jacaranda grounds to prevent NASA's memorial service.
Police lobbed teargas on Tuesday to disperse hundreds of Jubilee Party supporters outside Moi Sports Centre Kasarani where Kenyatta's oath was taking place (Nairobi - Kasarani).

Police and NASA supporters clashed when police tried to block a NASA Memorial Service, held for the victims of political violence. A 7 year old boy, a pregnant woman, and a demonstrator were killed by police bullets. Several people were injured.

Kenya's security forces on Monday destroyed six Al-Shabaab training camps in an ongoing operation to flush out militants from the vast Boni forest in the coastal town of Lamu. 'Many' Al-Shabaab militants were killed and others injured during the operation.

Detonation: An explosive thrown from a moving car hit the perimeter wall of a church, causing a security scare in Mandera Town. The device, according to an eyewitness, exploded immediately after the speeding Toyota Probox turned at a corner.

A group of illegal fishermen attacked and seriously injured four police officers at Lake Naivasha on Sunday. The officers had been confiscating illegal fishing gear near Malewa bay when the group armed with crude weapons descended on them.
Women in Garissa held a peaceful march to demonstrate their commitment to preventing gender based violence.

Three student from Isiolo Barracks Secondary School are in police custody after they allegedly attacked a soldier. The Form Four students were passing through the gate from their school after doing their national examinations when they assaulted the officer and caused disturbance.

Laikipia University students at Nakuru campus on Thursday morning staged a protest after their colleague was knocked down and killed by a vehicle. The students barricaded the busy Nakuru-Nairobi highway at Mbaruk using twigs and stones disrupting traffic. Police used teargas to disperse the rowdy students who paralysed transport on the highway for 30 minutes.

'A truck contracted by a UN agency partner in Garissa county ran over an IED planted in the road. All three contracted employees sustained major injuries as a result of the attack. Although no group claimed responsibility for the attack, the area is prone to extremist activities by Al-Shabaab. The workers were delivering food commodities at the time.'

Police lobbed teargas to disperse protesters at Uhuru Park (Nairobi - Westlands) on Wednesday. Reto Women Association was holding a peaceful demonstration to decry alleged police killing of over 300 livestock belonging to pastoralist communities who had invaded private ranches in Laikipia County.

At least 10 houses were torched early on Monday in Mirere village, Matungu sub-county, after a boda boda rider was killed on Sunday night. Following the incident, over 50 people have been rendered homeless.
NTV and other leading TV stations also broadcast footage of large crowds in President Uhuru Kenyatta's strongholds in Rift Valley regions celebrating the Supreme Court ruling.

notes: Protesters took to the street in opposition areas in the capital and the west of the country against a court decision. A paramedic tending the injured at a demonstration in western Migori was shot dead.

Police dispersed a crowd of protesters in the Korogocho settlement in the capital, Nairobi (Nairobi - Ruaraka) (coded separately). On 19 November 2017, opposition supporters engaged police in running battles in many parts of Nairobi as they protested the killing of five people by Mungiki.
Clashes erupted in Nairobi's Mathare slum on Sunday after four bodies were found in the street, with outrage spreading to Kibera.
Unidentified attackers shot at a bus that was travelling from Merti to Isiolo, killing 8 passengers.
A NASA supporter was killed in Kibera.

Students at the Athi River campus of Daystar University held a silent protest against the administration. The protest degenerated into violent demonstrations, which were broken up by the police. The university has closed both the Athi River campus and the Nairobi campus in response.

At least five people were killed Friday in confrontations between Kenyan police and supporters of opposition leader Raila Odinga as tensions over the disputed presidential election continued. Rioters are deemed responsible of many acts of violence, inculding sexual violence and property desruption. Eyewitnesses said police shot them. 'There were 15 bodies at the City mortuary and three at Chiromo mortuary when we visited. These people were shot by the gun and cartridges collected,' claimed Raila.

NASA supporters waiting at the airport for the return of Odinga clashed with the police. The police fired teargas to disperse the crowd and the demonstrators threw rocks. The police tried to block Odinga's convoy from travelling into Nairobi.

Kenyatta University has been closed indefinitely following a night of riots by students. There are reports that a huge fire broke out in one of the buildings in the institution (Nairobi - Starehe).The University's Vice Chancellor Prof Paul Wainaina announced on Friday morning that the decision was prompted by the ongoing lecturers' strike that had ' heightened agitation among students'.

Embakasi East MP Babu Owino, his Rauaraka counterpart TJ Kajwang and Starehe politician Steve Mbogo were arrested Thursday as Opposition leaders engaged police in a cat-and-mouse game. The leaders were apprehended on Ngong' Road (Nairobi - Westlands) as they attempted to enter Kibra's Kamkunji ground where NASA had scheduled a rally that had been banned by the police.

Property destruction: A church at the centre of a land tussle was destroyed on 15 November at Jogoo area in Kisii Town. Church officials said hired goons descended on Millennium SDA Church and vandalised it.

The hearing of a petition challenging the election of Homa Bay Governor Cyprian Awiti was adjourned for more than 30 minutes after supporters of two opposing groups clashed. Governor Awiti's supporters of and those of former Kasipul MP Oyugi Magwanga fought outside the Homa Bay High Court Tuesday morning.

Three police officers were killed on Tuesday. A team of police officers were headed back to a settlement called Lomelo from Kapedo where they delivered food rations to police camps when bandits sprayed their vehicle with bullets, killing the officers. A group of officers sent for reinforcement and rescue their colleagues were also caught up in the ambush, which left 10 with injuries and one missing.

At least eleven houses have been razed at Esoit in Trans Mara as renewed fighting between Kipsigis and Maasai communities erupted. No fatalities following the incident as residents of Bogoria Village had temporarily abandoned their homes following prolonged insecurity.
Students in Rachuonyo rioted when their teachers prevented them from cheating in the exams. The police intervened to break up the riots.
2 people were killed by police reservists in Basargeisa, in Bura.

Three women in Kitui were allegedly tortured by police on claims of insulting a local church leader. Mrs Hellen Kyalo, Ms Janet Mwikali and Mrs Kathini Mwema from Syongila Village in Kitui Central on Friday said the officers inflicted serious injuries on their behind, thighs and legs.
A woman who stabbed her boyfriend to death after a dispute over a phone was lynched by a mob in Murang'a Thursday morning.

Beneficiaries of government-allocated land clashed with squatters in Taveta. Eye witnesses report that 2 people were killed by bows and arrows in the clashes, although the authorities deny these deaths.
Residents of Narok protested against the rising insecurity.
University dons tried to hold a peaceful demonstration in Nairobi, but were threatened by the police, who confiscated their megaphones and blocked the road so that the march could not pass.

Transport in Mandera County has been paralysed after operators suspended bus services in the county for three days after al-Shabab attacked two police vehicles on Monday evening. Al-Shabab militants ambushed and burnt down two police land cruisers in an attack in Daba City, Mandera County on Monday. The two vehicles carrying police officers were escorting a bus to Mandera when they were hit by rocket-propelled grenades. 12 killed, several wounded.

The KDF intercepted an Al Shabaab group of militants who was heavily armed and planning to carry out attacks in Lamu West on Thursday. An operation (Linda Boni) was called to capture the militants who escaped during the gun battle into the Boni forest. During the incident, six AK-47 assault rifles, 321 bullets, three grenades and explosives were recovered.

Police were patrolling the private ranches in Ol Moran and Ratia and were attacked by the pastoralists when they tried to evict them. There was an exchange of fire between the officers and the pastoralists who were all armed. The latter destroyed a vehicle, after which the police countered with fire in a 2-hour long battle.
Al Shabaab militants attacked a land cruiser in Arabia. They stole the land cruiser and shot at the passengers. 2 passengers were injured.
Al Shabaab militants hijacked a car and abducted a driver between Fino and Sheikh Barrow. He is alive, but being held in Somalia.

Transport along Kericho-Kisumu Highway on Tuesday was disrupted after matatu owners blocked the road near Parkmatt supermarket protesting vandalism of their two vehicles. Anti-riot police fired teargas to disperse the protesters. Some vehicle passengers were injured in the process. The vehicles were allegedly vandalised near Chemelil trading center in Kisumu County by NASA supporters who were protesting the announcement of Uhuru Kenyatta as the winner of repeat presidential election.

In Kisumu, angry youth held demonstrations in Kondele, the main bus station and Nairobi Road complaining about the 866 votes said to have been cast in Kisumu. They lit bonfires, blocked roads and, in some cases, extorted money from motorists.

In Nairobi, several groups of supporters marched through the city's main streets singing and chanting to celebrate the win of newly-confirmed President Kenyatta. The same happened in other locations. In Narok, however, two men from different communities clashed, leaving 5 people injured.
In the slums of Kibra, in Nyamira, youth lit bonfires to protest against the election of Kenyatta.
A Land Cruiser carrying five passengers was attacked by Al Shabaab militants at Arabia area. The driver was released and two passengers suffered gunshot wounds but they were in stable condition.
Police dispersed Jubilee supporters in Mumias.

The altercation between the police and protesters at the Majengo bus stage began when a car belonging to a local businessman was allegedly found with marked presidential election ballot papers. One person was shot and at least 11 others were injured. Among those beaten up was a police in civilian uniform who ran to the scene.

A group of young people tried to prevent Cabinet Secretary Matiangi from leaving the Gatina Primary School. The cabinet secretary had moved to address the crowd when people started chanting 'Matiang'i must go!'. Police used tear gas to disperse the agitated crowd that had started pelting stones at CS Matiang'i's motorcade, and then the school. Pupils who attempted to leave the school's premises got caught up in clashes, some being rendered unconscious while others gasped for air.
Violence broke out in Kibera when the winner of the election run-off was declared. NASA supporters rioted and set tires alight. The police tried to break up the protests.
One man was found dead in a sugar cane plantation one day after ethnic tensions between the Luo and Kalenjin communities got into an ethnic clash. The body had been hacked with a panga.
Kenyan police have used tear gas to disperse opposition supporters who threw stones after a government official visited a school in Kawangware.

Movement of forces: on 29 October, armed men from Waithaka and Ndonyo area raided Kabiria. Young men were armed with pangas and threatened to conduct a door-to-door search to flush out Luos and Luhyas, who they said were living on their land. No actual violence reported.
Non-violent activity: Villagers from the Luo and Kalenjin communities armed themselves against each other on 28 October in Kisumu County.
Rioters demonstrated in the town of Majengo. They were incited to attack a car which was said to have ballot papers, but after damaging it, it was not confirmed.
3 police officers mistaken for protesters were beaten on Saturday afternoon by other police forces in Majengo Town during ongoing demonstrations.
Kenyan police have used tear gas in an attempt to disperse crowds of opposition supporters in the Nairobi slum of Kawangware.
Police gunned down three men suspected of having killed the two police officers. They also recovered the stolen weapons and the AK-47s. The fighting lasted for 5 hours.
Angry protesters took to the streets, blocking roads to protest the decision to redo the elections on Saturday in certain counties.

A man was shot dead while two others suffered gunshot wounds last Friday when they attempted to torch Mr Rege's home in Pala Village in Karachuonyo Constituency. Mr Rege confided to journalists that he suspected the MCAs were behind the plans to torch his home over allegations that there were ballot papers in his home marked in favour of President Uhuru Kenyatta.
Youth attacked election officials at Bogwo polling station in Muhoroni. They also attacked and beat voters.
Protesters took to the streets again to show their opposition to holding elections on Saturday. Outside Kisumu's morgue, 30 women stood weeping with signs saying 'Stop killing our sons'.
Angry protesters took to the streets, blocking roads to protest the decision to redo the elections on Saturday in certain counties. Rioters got into clashes with the police.

The police opened fire on protesters who were demonstrating against the decision to hold elections again on Saturday and killed two of them in Bungoma. The demonstrators blocked the road and lit fires.

Police raided houses of civilians in Kisumu, beating civilians and injuring dozens. Live bullets were used on some civilians, including a 14 year old boy. Of the 29 people injured, 26 had suffered gun shots.

Non-violent activity: In Chakol estate in Busia, police threw teargas cannisters into houses to flush out the inhabitants. They claimed to be searching for the youth who had disrupted the voting the previous day. No reported injuries.
A 17-year old is shot in the chest and injured during violent demonstrations in Sindo town.
In Migori the police stormed residential estates, where they fired teargas into homes, beat people, and raped women. 1 man was killed when he was shot in the head.
2 Kenyan police officers are killed during an ambush in Nairobi. The attackers were armed with AK47s and they stole the officers weapons after killing them with shots from the back.

As a revenge to the previous event, the Kikuyu joined forces and attacked the Luo. The ethnic tensions and violence led to one severely injured person. Residents claims three were killed and dozens, including three school children, were injured.

Rioters started throwing stones at the police in the morning, during the demonstrations against the elections to be held the next day. The police responded with teargas and water cannons. The rioters were mostly from the Luo ethnic group and they took the opportunity to loot several stores, attack residents and to burn a store owned by an ethnic Kikuyu. One woman was raped.
Residents kept off polling stations, choosing instead to protest an attack on Kisima Primary School polling station by a senior administration officer last Wednesday.
Young people pretending to be voters disturb the voting polls in Narok.
A crowd sets tyres on fire to protest the presidential election vote.
One man was stabbed in the neck in Likoni, Mombasa. It is not yet certain whether he was attacked on the way to vote.
Opposition supporters in Turkana county burned election materials to protest the election run-off.
Angry villagers who saw that a teacher had marked ballot papers gathered to set fire to his house. The civilian had already sought refuge.
In Mombassa, demonstrators lit tyres and timbers along the main highway.
A Returning Officer was attacked by demonstrators in Migori town on his way to the polling centre. He sustained slight injuries and lost a number of his personal items.

A 13-year-old was shot on his way to a kiosk in Sofia Slum, while a man was shot in Makadara Shopping centre. Police arrest 35 protesters who were barricading roads and disturbing the voting polls in Kakamega.

In North Karachuonyo, youths were repulsed after attempting to enter the home of former MP James Rege. Police say there were no injuries but reports indicate a man was shot and two others injured during the incident. One of them died of his wounds.
In Rangwe market, a police officer, who was escorting ballot boxes was injured after he was hit by a stone thrown by protesting youths.
Rioters/youth clash with police in Kakamega town. During the riots, a police officer mistakenly shot a National Youth Service officer in Kakamega.

In Bungoma County, violent riots erupted in Kimilili, Chwele and Webuye leading to confrontations with police officers. Youths use bees to keep voters away from Matsakha polling station and are eventually dispersed by police.

At Mugai Primary School, an assistant chief was chased away by angry locals who accused him of dishing handouts to coerce people to vote. Locals said the officer was giving people perceived to be Jubilee supporters Sh50 and directing them to the polling station to cast their ballots.

In Busia, a group of boda boda drivers stormed a polling station and burnt ballot boxes, forms 32A, 33, 34A, 41, supervisor validation forms, ballot papers, IEBC stamps, badges and reflector jackets, and stole two gas lanterns and cylinders.
Opposition supporters barricaded the roads in Busia with burning tires. The police fired live ammunition to disperse the crowds. At least 5 people were injured.
Within Murumba market, youths attacked an army truck that was ferrying goods from the Hakati Army Camp. The army officers fired in the air dispersing the youths.

A group of about 200 rowdy youths from neighbouring Siaya County attacked a polling station by throwing stones. In the process, one ballot box containing ballot papers was destroyed. Police moved in quickly and restored order.
In St. Marys Bangladesh, rowdy youths blocked the entrance to the polling centre forcing the IEBC officials to suspend the exercise while arrangements were made to manage the situation.

ANC party representative's supporters protested against the Independent Electoral Commission (IEBC) after the candidate's name was missing from the IEBC register list.

A man was shot dead by a gang in Mai Mahiu on 26/05/2017. The police has yet to establish the motive of the killing.
Violence broke out as hundreds of K'Oyoo's supporters, lit twigs and blocked roads to protest the absence of his name as a candidate on the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC)s.
Three Al-Shabaab militants shot dead a Tana River County Assembly driver on Friday

Two people were injured after supporters of Tharaka-Nithi Governor Samuel Ragwa and Chuka/Igambang'ombe MP Muthomi Njuki clashed at Marimanti town. Youth in Oyugis rioted at the campaign rally of the Homa Bay governor. The police dispersed the crowd with teargas.
Women protest demanding a man accused of sodomising local children be convicted and jailed.

At least three policemen were killed in an IED explosions in Liboi, Garissa County, near the Kenya - Somalia border. Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility of the attacks.

Presiding Officers (POs) and clerks who oversaw Jubilee party's primaries took to the streets of Kericho town to protest the party's bureaucracy and delays in paying them their salaries.

Traders protested demolition of their stalls in Mombasa on 23/05/2017. They barricaded a road with logs and bonfires. The anti-riot team of the Kenyan police forces used tear gas to disperse the demonstrators. No fatalities.

Youths at an ODM meeting in Kakamega assaulted Nation journalist Linet Wafula and destroyed her phone. No serious injuries reported.

Al Shabaab militants raided Omar Jilo, in northern Kenya, where they clashed with police forces. 2 local administrators were killed and 2 police reservists were abducted. Security personnel are pursuing the attackers.

At least six Kenyan security officers were injured in a bomb blast on Monday in the northeast region of Garissa near the Somali border. Somali militant group Al-Shabaab has claimed responsibility for the attack, saying its fighters killed four government soldiers, including two commanders.
Dan Ocholla, a journalist at The Standard, was attacked and seriously injured by Kakamega County soldiers while taking photos of injured workers at a construction site in the town.

Ngecha residents demonstrated on 07/05/2017 urging the government to prevent crime in the area. The demonstration was sparked by recent murders.

Violent protests and running battles with police occurred in Dandora after police shot a deaf boy they mistook for a robbery suspect. Injuries as a result of the protest are not known.

Supporters for different aspirants for the Jubilee ticket in Ruiru clash.

The aspiring ODM Naivasha candidate was arrested and held, and then admitted to hospital.

ODM supporters of John Mbadi clash with those of Caroli Omondi at a party rally in Magunga on 17/04. Two reported injuries.
Supporters of two governor primary candidates (Joseph Ole Lenku and Tarayia Ole Kores) of the Jubilee party clashed on 17/04/2017 in Namanga. Seven people were injured but there were no fatalities.

Protests broke out in Kabete, Kiambu County on 15/04 following the disappearance of a parliamentary aspirant. The politician was reported missing the previous night, while his car, riddled with bullet holes, was found early Saturday in Gitaru. The fate of his person is not known.
ODM party has cancelled nomination results for Khwisero constituency due to irregularities, resulting in protests. No reports of violence
In Migori, unidentified youths invaded a rally in Sori Town on Saturday evening, forcing ODM activist Peter Jobando, a licensed firearm holder, to fire in the air several times.

Supporters of MP Paul Otuoma of ODM protested the announcement of provisional results of the ODM Busia Governor nominations. Supporters shouted at the chairman of the county elections board and security agents had to take two men out of the hall, where the results where announced.
Two suspected Islamist militants are killed in an extra-judicial killing by unidentified assailants in Naivasha. Both were suspected of recruiting and funding 'terror' activities.

A female Jubilee aspirant who is running for Tetu parliamentary seat, is attacked by four masked men armed with metal bars and a gun at Mbaaini village.
There were intense firefights between Pokot militias and government forces near Olmaiso, in Laikipia.

Pokot raiders attacked Matweku police post in Ol Ari Nyiro Nature Conservancy, killing a police officer and abducting two others on 13/04/2017. Later the captured policemen were found dead at Kamwenje in Baringo. It is believed that the policemen were killed by Pokots.
A police officer and a civilian died in a firefight between Pokot militias and government forces near Olmaiso, in Laikipia, on 13/04/2017.
Dozens of Kisumu residents protested over an alleged plot by the government to auction a local Sh4.2 billion mall.
ODM nominations in Busia County turned, with Deputy Governor Kizito Wangalwa's vehicle being smashed, its tires deflated and the driver attacked by rioting youth.
In Tharaka-Nithi, two supporters of Governor Samuel Ragwa were injured during the launch of Chuka/Igambangombe MP Muthomi Njuki's manifesto on April 12.
At least seven Pokot were killed by police during a security operation in Tiaty, Baringo County. The gunmen were allegedly planning a livestock raid.
Non-violent activity: 10 April, 23:00EAT, Mandera, Kenya: al Shabaab militants entered Mandera and hijacked two pick-up trucks.
In a crackdown on 'banditry', police set fire to a Pokot village. An infant dies during the raid.
Raiders kill one person in Pokot north during a peace meeting
4 people are killed by herders in Nakwomuru village in central Pokot county. Police reservists engage with the raiders, killing three of them.
One person is feared dead and scores injured after supporters of Funyula MP Paul Otuoma and Busia Governor Sosepeter Ojamoong clashed in Funyula over the ODM primaries
4 people are killed by herders in Nakwomuru village in central Pokot county. Police reservists engage with the raiders, killing three of them
Sex workers in Mombasa staged a protest after a colleague was murdered by a client.
Angry and rowdy youth chanting anti-Jubilee slogans disrupted the president's rally in Wajir and engaged the police. The police dispersed the rioters.

Nominated Senator Elizabeth Ongoro led her supporters to protest the direct nomination handed to her rival at Orange House, the ODM headquarters in Nairobi (Nairobi - Westlands). A plain clothed security officer was forced to shoot in the air to disperse the rowdy youths who had stormed the party Headquarters and were roughing up ODM Executive Director Oduor Ongwen.
Sex workers protest at the deputy county commissioner's office demanding justice after a murder of a colleague.
Pokot gunmen open fire at Ol Moran livestock market in bid to steal cattle. There are no references to injuries. But the police engage the gunmen in a battle later. No deaths reported
Factions of ODM members clash during a rally. He groups were divided over support of Governor Zachary Okoth Obado and gubernatorial candidate Ochillo Ayacko.
The car of ODM politician Hassan Joho was attacked by gunmen. Joho's bodyguard was shot and injured but no fatalities is reported. Joho claims it to be an attempt of assassination.
Unidentified arsonists petrol-bombed the Migori ODM offices ahead of a party rally the following day.
Two Administration Police officers were attacked and set ablaze in Voi at the weekend when they were mistaken to be thugs.

Residents of Kisumu protested peacefully over a delay in the opening of a mall. The opening has been delayed by ambiguities of bank loan payments. The protest was led by the director of Youth Reconciliation Forum of Kenya Eric Okello.
Video released on socia media shows a police kill an unarmed man in Eastleigh on 31/03/2017. The victim was suspected of killing two police officers last month.
Movement of forces: Suspected Al-Shabaab hijacked a Kenyan government vehicle in the border town of Elwak in Mandera country. The attackers released the driver and reportedly drove into Somalia.

Property destruction: Suspected 'cattle herders' burn down a tourist lodge on the Laikipia Plateau. The herders may have torched the lodge in retaliation to an ongoing security operation in the area. The hotel was empty at the time of the attack.
When police blocked Hassan Joho's supporters and the press from following him into the police headquarters, the supporters protested in the streets of Mombasa.
Mukutan Lodge was attacked by herders seeking pasture. They exchanged gunfire with the security forces and burned down the lodge.
A young boy is killed by armed raiders involved in a boundary dispute. It is not known in the victim was specifically targeted. Exact date not clear - source dated 28/03.
Beach operators protest against a competitor's construction of a sea wall.
Two unidentified neighbouring communities clash in Garissa, along its border with Wajir over a boundary dispute. One bystander was reportedly killed in the clash. Date not clear - source dated 28/03.
A boda boda driver on the Jubilee campaign was stabbed to death by a fellow campaigner over campaign payments. Attacker assumed to be Jubilee.
Kenyans in Namanga [border town] demonstrated against Tanzanian leader John Magufuli on Monday [27 March], saying he had deported their counterparts.

Violence erupted in a political rally of the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) on 27/03/2017 in Kendu Bay. Supporters of two rival politicians of the same party, Governor Cyprian Awiti and Mr. Oyugi Magwanga, clashed injuring three people. No fatalities.

Attackers believed to be from the Bahgere clan from Wajir South attacked Fadiwein village, which is inhabited by Auliyan community, injuring one. Eleven houses were also burnt and the attackers made away with 300 goats and five camels. The two communities had been fighting over a disputed boundary with the Bahgere, claiming the area falls under Wajir South, while Auliyan says it is in Garissa county.

On 19/03 in Mukutani, four police officers were wounded when suspected Pokot herdsmen fired on their vehicle as they escorted members of the Ilchamus community to safety.
Kenya's president deployed the military to quell violence related to drought.
Lawmakers in the Mandera County Assembly clash over disagreements of a bill. Political parties not known.
Students at a Maseno school go on 'rampage' over disagreements of their institution's leadership.

Protest in the Rhamu over a proposed county budget.
