Related, on 04/03, a police helicopter was shot at in the same farm as security officers carried out aerial surveillance. A second source claims the attack took place on 6 March.
On 04/03, a police helicopter was shot at by Pokot or Samburu raidersas security officers carried out aerial surveillance.
Property destruction: A UK national's home that had been burnt down by Pokot or Samburu raiders on 03/03.
Unidentified gunmen kidnapped three teachers from Dadaab camp. Al Shabaab have carried out abductions in the past, though it is not clear who the perpetrators were in this instance.

Eight are dead in clashes between Tugen-Ilchamus and Pokot clans during the weeks of 26/02-12/03, exact dates, location and other details not known. Accounting for the activity between the clans in the present week, the fatality total stands at 21.

Traders and hawkers clashed on 01/03. A court order released on 24 February by the Milimani Commercial Courts had allowed the return of hawkers to trade on two streets in Eastleigh. Traders however protested the court's move leading to Wednesday's clashes.

Jubilee Party youths opposed to the National Super Alliance (Nasa) have blocked Raila Odinga and Kalonzo Musyoka from addressing a rally at a scheduled venue. The mob on Monday used rocks to barricade the entrance to Meru town main stage, forcing the two leaders to keep off.
Protest against the state of roads block traffic in Kayole.
Security forces kill a suspected al Shabaab member in Kwale and recover weapons.
A 45-year-old man was lynched on the weekend (25-26 February) when neighbours found him sleeping with the corpse of his 15 year old daughter in Molo Township.

Three suspected remnants of the Sabaot Land Defence Force were on 24/02 lynched by residents in Cheptais, Mt Elgon. The attackers also torched the suspects' houses. The attackers suspected the three recently murdered a man.
Three are killed in clashes over land in the Athi River area. Following, police made 92 arrests.
Boda boda riders in Maralal Town held demonstrations over alleged misappropriation of funds meant for construction of shades.

Security Measures: More than 30 schools have been closed due to persistent attacks by armed Pokot militia in Baringo county. Closed schools include Ngaratuko, Chemoe, Yatya, Tuluk, Kagir, Loruk, Chepkesin, Kapturo, Toboroi, Barsuswo and Lokorotabim in Baringo North.
Clinical officers in Narok County on 22/02 staged demonstrations and camped outside the county headquarters demanding promotions and harmonisation of their salaries.
Three are attacked and killed with blunt objects in Garissa on the night of 22/02. Perpetrators not known.
On 22 February 2017, one person was shot dead in Loruk by Pokot militants as 400 residents fled after their homes were set on fire.

On 22 February 2017, police found the bodies of four men in a vehicle in Gitaru. Police said they appeared to have been strangled to death and had visible injuries in their necks and faces. The reason for their deaths was not established.
On 22 February 2017, a teacher was killed by Pokot militants in Chepkesin in Baringo North.
Striking universities lecturers hold a peaceful demonstrations in Nairobi to demand implementation of a 2013-2017 collective bargaining agreement.
Kilif nurses protest unpaid allowances.
Two more people were killed in Baringo county in attacks by armed Pokot militants. Specific details not provided.
On 19 February 2017, Pokot militants killed a young mother and her three-year old child at Natan in Baringo North. Another source reported that the attack took place on 21 February.

Residents of Nakuru took to the streets to protest the ownership of a piece of land in Mwariki. Police dispersed the more than 100 residents of Mutegi Estate who had blocked the Nakuru-Kiambogo road using stones.
On 18 February 2017, two local leaders, MCA Kibet Cheretei and a Jubilee MP hopeful Pepe Kitambaa were shot dead by Pokot militants at a bar in Marigat town.
A fight between a Pokot and Marakwet near Kerio River led to the death of one.

On 17 February 2017, four people were seriously injured after suspected Pokot assailants attacked a bus carrying former Inspector General David Kimaiyo's relatives. The attack occurred on the Chesongoch-Liter road, near Tot trading centre.

Armed youths disrupt an ODM rally in Katilia. Opposition leader Raila Odinga was speaking at the time of the attack. The youths were accused of being incited by MPs to disrupt the event. Police fired in the air to disperse the crowd. Injuries not known.
On 14 February 2017, university lecturers protested in Nairobi after doctors were jailed for refusing to call off their strike. They are also protesting over low wages.
On 14 February 2017, police fired teargas to disperse protesting youth from Mathare who barricaded the road over claims of illegal voter registration.
County workers protest a breach of government contract by dumping sewage at a county office.
Residents clash with police in Mugumoini village over a land surveying issue. A man was shot and injured.
At least 12 houses were torched in Pimbinyiet, Trans Mara West after clashes between two communities lasted over two days.
A police officer was hacked to death at Mangala in Makueni County by a group of sand harvesters over the right to land.
At least 12 houses were torched in Pimbinyiet, Trans Mara West after clashes between two communities lasted over two days.
Residents protest in Subukia after a student is killed the previous day by 'thugs.'
Youths protest during an address by the Kisii governor at Ekona. The demonstrators were demanding better government services.
On 8 February 2017, an 82-year-old man who is the uncle of Kapseret MP was shot dead by heavily armed militants who raided his home in Kerio Valley.

On 8 February 2017, a 43-year-old man was hacked to death in a dispute between two factions of a family over land in Kinangop, Nyandarua county. Four attackers, armed with pangas attacked the family home.
On 8 February 2017, Samburu residents protested against Raila Odinga, burning posters and lighting bonfires.

Herders, illegally trespassing on land, injure a police officer and burn homes in Miteta, Ng'arua Division in Laikipia when they were confronted by a police. The violence comes 24 hours after a similar confrontation near Rumuruti.
Police shoot in the air and lob teargas canisters to disperse violent residents of Simba Chai in Teso South, Busia County who were protesting after they were allegedly denied national Identity cards.
Armed herders trespassing on illegal land shoot and injure a police officer after they were confronted near Rumuruti.
On 6 February 2017, a protest was held over the death of a motorist who was hit by a speeding vehicle. Protesters called on the government to erect speed bumps.
Two public service vehicles were on 04/02 burnt down along Lang'ata Road in Nairobi - Langata by rioters after several had been in area accidents.

On 3 February 2017, Eunice Wambui (aka Nyasuguta from Vitimbi), an actress who has been campaigning to become the MP for Embakasi South, was beaten with wooden rods by four political goons in Mukuru Kwa Ruben.

100+ gunmen believed to be al-Shabaab attacked a police post and destroyed communication masts in Arabia area, Mandera County. At least one bystander died in the attack. Number of other casualties not known, as al Shabaab had destroyed communication masts in the area. Shabelle Media Network reports an 'unknown number of police officers were killed.'
Tea farmers on Kirinyaga protest against the sale of company land. Location not known.
On 29 January 2017, two suspected criminals were stoned to death by villagers at Othoro marke, Rachuonyo East subcounty.
Protesters force an ODM rally in Changamwe to end prematurely.
National Alliance supporters, specifically that of Senator Mike Sonko, attack journalists covering a visit from the Governor. Injuries reported. The attack occurred on or before 25/01.
Youth in Isiolo Town protest over what they termed as delays in the vetting process for issuing national identification cards.
A Kenya Police Reservist (KPR) was killed after suspected Al-Shabaab perpetrators hurled explosives at a bank and two hotels in Mandera town on the morning of 23/01.
A group of vigilantes attack and kill two they suspect of robbery.
On 22 January 2017, residents in Kitungati village (Kitui) blocked police from removing the body of a man killed the day before by Somali militants.
Three are killed in a land dispute in Kanyakwar. The following day a group protest at the office of the 'assistant chief', claiming he 'had a hand in the dispute.'
On 21 January 2017, suspected Somali militia shot dead a herder in Ukasi, Kitui county.

On 21 January 2017, a man was shot in the waist and a woman was beaten after police clashed with squatters on disputed land in Nguu Tatu, Kisauni constituency, Mombasa. The squatters threw stones and shot arrows at police who lobbed teargas canisters to disperse them.
Three are killed in a land dispute in Kanyakwar. The following day a group protest at the office of the 'assistant chief', claiming he 'had a hand in the dispute.'

On 19 January 2017, Egerton University lecturers protested in Nakuru. Lecturers in several parts of the country defied a court order and began their strike for the government to implement a 2013 pay rise agreement.

On 19 January 2017, Machakos University lecturers protested on Makueni-Machakos road. Lecturers in several parts of the country defied a court order and began their strike for the government to implement a 2013 pay rise agreement. Machakos University lecturers protested on Makueni-Machakos road.
On 19 January 2017, medical students in Nairobi protested disruptions to their studies during the doctors' strike.

Residents engaged police and Kenya Wildlife officers in running battles for most of Wednesday after a resident was killed by an elephant who had invaded a farm at Sironi village, Laikipia West Sub-County. The residents barricaded the busy Nyahururu-Ng'arua road at Maili Saba junction, causing a gridlock. The group demanded the government construct an electrified fence to protect them from further attacks.
Two woman who were accused of witchcraft are lynched in Nyamokenye village, Nyamira on the evening of 14/01.

A suspect behind a spate of motorbike theft and rape cases was Friday lynched in Kelonget village in Bomet Central. Irate public set the man's house blaze before stoning him to death and setting his body on fire after an extended search.
Non-violent activity: Heavily armed Somali militia/herders are reported to have encorached onto farms in Kitui, armed with AK-47s and displaced unprotected farmer settlements.

A group of angered boda boda operators attack a full passenger bus, setting it alight. The boda boda rider were angered after a colleague was injured in an accident. All passengers escaped, no casualties.

A bystander student was killed on Sunday as renewed clashes between the Kipsigis and Maasai communities escalated at Pimbinyiet on the Trans Mara West-Trans Mara East border in Narok County. A similar clash took place at the location on 04/01.

Busia County residents have destroyed properties in protest to the killing of a boda boda rider by a police officer. torched a police Land Cruiser and four houses (three belonging to Administration Police officers and one for the chief). The driver had been shot during a traffic stop.
One is dead following clashes between Kipsigis and Maasai militias at Pimbinyiet on the Trans Mara West-Trans Mara East border in Narok County.

Residents blocked the Nyeri-Karatina road to protest rising accidents. The residents barricaded the road using stones and bonfires and urged the Kenya National Highway Authority to erect speed bumps to reduce the number of accidents.
On 2 January 2017, Somali militants shot dead two herders in Inyanzae.
Residents block roads in protest of pollution of a nearby river.
A Kipsigis man is dead and others are injured following an attack from suspected Maasai militia at Esoit, Junction and Kirindon in Trans Mara West. Similar violence had occurred in recent weeks.

Non-violent activity: Pokot bandits have resorted to blocking roads using twigs and stones. Currently, they have barricaded Makutani-Arabal road, Norokwei-Kiserian road and speculation is high that they are likely to close the Arabal-Sirata road in a bid to block security officers from flushing them out of their hideouts.

One person was killed on the night of 26/12 while three others sustained serious injuries following an attack by suspected Pokot militia in Chesongoch, Kerio Valley. A similar attack occurred earlier in the week.
On 26 December 2016, 20 people were injured as residents from Matundura and Gituro villages (Naivasha and Kinangop constituencies) clashed over a boundary dispute.
Non-violent activity: on 25 December, a group of suspected Pokot militia raided a village near Arabel and forced locals who were attending a church service to flee. No one was injured.
On 24 December 2016, Somali militants who have encroached Kitui county and posing as herders, gunned down a man in Katangini.
On 24 December 2016, one person was shot and injured when suspected Pokot militia raided Chemwoyo and Murkutwo. Marakwet herders retaliated leading to an hour of heavy gunfire.
At least two people were killed and some others injured by suspected al-Shabaab who vandalized a communication mast in the Tarbaj area near the border with Somalia.

One attacker died and three police officers were wounded Friday after a group of men armed with machetes and bows assaulted a coastal police post to steal guns, an official said. No group has claimed responsibility, but initial suspicion has fallen on a secessionist group called the Mombasa Republican Council that wants the coastal region to secede from Kenya, claiming marginalization.
Lawmakers from major opposition parties in Kenya staged a walkout from a parliamentary session to protest the passage of a contentious legal provision.

Three people were on 21/12 are killed in Esoit, Trans Mara West (outside Kilgoris) in Narok County as fighting between the Kipsigis and Maasai communities. The fighting was an escalation of tit-for-tat attacks the previous day.
More than 600 demonstrators from Sagalla in Taita Taveta County on 20/12 blocked the Nairobi-Mombasa highway to protest against increased cases of human-wildlife conflict in the area.
A Kipsigis is killed by people believed to be from the Maasai community outside Kilgoris at Esoit trading centre. The attack led to retaliation from Kipsigs militia.
Members of a Kipsigs militia attack and kill two Maasai in retaliation for earlier violence.

On 20 December 2016, interclan skirmishes were reported in the Kerio Valley. This is a continuation from the previous day. 25 houses were burned and two people were killed in total in the attacks. Fatalities coded on 19 December.

Pokot raiders attack and kill a crossing guard during in Liter village and two others in neighbouring Endo Location, both in the Kerio valley the early morning hours. The attacks led to ethnic tension in the area.

notes: Police use tear gas and clash electoral commission protesters during a protest in Nairobi. Reports of excessive violence reported from police. Fifteen arrests reported.
Residents attack and kill a suspected robber in Buruburu on 15/04.

assoc_actor_1: CORD: Coalition for Reforms and Democracy
notes: In Kwale, a group of opposition CORD supporters made their way to the IEBC offices in Diani, Msambweni Sub-County, peacefully handed a letter to the assistant returning officer Mwamize Achani and left. Source dated 10/05.

assoc_actor_1: CORD: Coalition for Reforms and Democracy
notes: A CORD protest in Kisumu is met with 'heavy police presence.' No reported violence. Exact date not known - source dated 10/05.

assoc_actor_1: CORD: Coalition for Reforms and Democracy
notes: Police disperse 'opposition protesters' at the offices of the electoral commission in Nairobi (Nairobi - Starehe) due to alleged bias and corruption. Police involvement began after many of the protesters began pelting the officers with stones.

A group of residents in Emurua Dikirr Constituency protest outside the Ward Administrators office over the poor state of the roads which led to a number of local deaths. Another group launches a counter protest at the same location and accuses the demonstrators of illegal protest and undermining the county leadership. There is no reports of violence between the two groups.
Businessman and prominent critic of the government Jacob Juma is shot dead by unknown gunmen in Nairobi. Nothing was stolen. The opposition has labelled his killing an assassination.
Police officers in Kasarani lobbed teargas to disperse hundreds of boda boda riders who had barricaded the Thika Superhighway at Roysambu, Kamiti protesting the death of a colleague.

assoc_actor_1: CORD: Coalition for Reforms and Democracy
notes: Protesting members of CORD are tear-gassed by police after they attempt to forcibly enter the offices of the electorial comission in Kisumu. CORD was attempting to 'kick out' the commissions officials.
Police tear-gas electorial reform protesters in Nairobi. Warning shots and tear gas was firied after the protest broke a police line.
Protesters burn the home of a Embu man suspected of child rape after he is released on bond.

Tens of business owners in Embu Town Wednesday (13/04) afternoon held a peaceful demonstration protesting alleged harassment by Kenya Bureau of Standards (Kebs) officials. [The demonstrators] marched to the Embu County government and county commissioners offices seeking to be addressed but were repulsed by police. Kebs officials had accused many of the traders of selling counterfeit items and threatened them with arrest.
Laikipia University students block roads to protest examination fees, causing the school to close.
Masinde Muliro University students protest examination fees, causing the school to temporarily close. No reported violence.
11 April. An unidentified armed group killed a civilian working in a trade union and ranch in Zimmerman, Nairobi. The killing is believed to have been in relation to the victims work on land rights.
Al Shabaab fighters attack a police station in Dif on 10/04, injuring three officers before escaping in the police vehicle.
Residents of Kirinyaga County protest a law that would move the counties headquarters. Date of protest not known - source dated 04/04.

assoc_actor_1: SONU: Students Organisation of Nairobi University; Students (Kenya)
notes: University of Nairobi students protest a dispute in a campus union poll, burn the Students Organisation of Nairobi University (Sonu) offices (Nairobi - Starehe) and block a section of University Way and Uhuru Highway before police used teargas to disperse them. The protest caused the school to temporally close.
Police use tear-gas to disperse a group of 'rowdy' matatu operators who blocked roads in downtown Nairobi ahead of a planned strike to protest parking license cancellation.

Members of the Akorino religious sect protest at 47 churches throughout Embu county over alleged discrimination after their children were sent home from school after refusing to remove their headgear.
A vigilante mob lynches and burns a suspected thief in Mariani on 29/03.

Following several high-speed automobile accidents in their area, residents of Mairo Inya erect several speed bumps on a thoroughfare. Following their action, a group of motorists stage a protest of the poor driving condition.
After a murder suspect is released by police he is attacked and killed by vigilantes in suburban Nairobi.

assoc_actor_1: SONU: Students Organisation of Nairobi University
notes: The Students Organisation of Nairobi University (SONU) chairman Babu Owino is charged with severely assaulting a fellow student during the height of the student elections.
Mombasa residents gather to protest a county plan to demolish old houses in their area.

Four members of a vigilante mob are shot and wounded when police opened fire on the group who were attempting to lynch a suspected thief. The vigilantes had chased the suspect into a house when the police opened fire to disperse them. One police officer was also reported injured.
Hundreds of women in Malindi staged a demonstration following an assault of a person during the recent parliamentary by-election.

Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology (JKUAT) students took to the streets in riot on 09/03 over the death of a student at the institution, for whom they blame a local hospital for negligence.

A group of Ethiopian nationals are attacked and nearly lynched in a Nairobi suburb by a vigilante mob who blame them for a recent murder of boda driver. The police were able to intervene before any bloodshed.
Supporters of KANU and police clash at the Moi Gardens location after police attempted to stop a political rally when the event space had been booked by another group.

A decision by the Narok County Government to close 15 camps in the Maasai Mara Game Reserve has sparked protests on 02/03 from the local community, mostly from tour operators and hoteliers who benefit from the tourism industry.
Militias from Maasai and Kalenjin clash over land at Kosovo in Naivasha (Mathare). Six houses destroyed, 1 killed and 1 injured.

Rioters block traffic at Olololunga, between Narok and Bomet after a motorist killed a number of cattle while speeding along the roadway. Anti-riot police came to the scene to 'contain the situation,' though it is not clear if the police engaged the protesters.

Cooperative farmers in Naivasha burn several houses in protest over 'malpractice' of land division. Police fired into the air to disperse the group. Earlier, the demonstrators had forced four primary schools and a secondary school to close down, with students joining them in the day-long demonstrations.

Chuka University students violently protest disputed school elections by looting shops and lighting fires. Police made 15 arrests and offices temporarily closed the university. The date(s) of the protest are not known. The election was held on 29/01, though it is not clear if protests immediately followed.
A vigilante group attacks and kills a man they suspect of murder in Eastleigh.
Taxi drivers violently protest the advent of Uber in the city. The drivers believe the ride sharing service will upset their business.
Residents of Ndagani protest the poor state of a road on 03/02, burning tyres.

Three people have been killed in a village in Baringo South Sub-County in an attack suspected to retaliatory following the killing of a man on Sunday. Suspected Ilchamus militants attacked Mbechot Village on Tuesday evening when residents were having a meeting with Sub-County Commissioner Felix Kisalu.
Residents engage in running battles with the police after the city confiscated a car wash machine from a business. No reported injury.
Al Shabaab attacks Pandanguo village, targeting the homes of Christians. Al Shabaab claimed 'many' killed, though more reliable reports indicate three dead, plus injuries.
On 31 January 2016, more than 400 residents of Mpeketoni in Lamu County (Lamu West) protested over increased insecurity and frequent attacks by Al-Shabaab militants.
An Ilchamus man is killed by a communal militia (suspected Tugen militia) in Olesampurmpur village in Baringo South.
Property destruction: A gang on the night of 31/01 raided Meru Governor Peter Munyas home and vandalised one of his official security cars. The governor was away, and was not harmed.
Six police (or seven - Shabelle Media Network) officers are killed when their vehicle struck an IED in Lamu, suspected al Shabaab responsible.
Laikipia University students riot following a released report recommending the closure of their school. Police fired tear gas and made several arrests.
The Anti-Terrorism Police Unit on [20 January] morning killed four al Shabaab after a shootout in Kwachocha, Malindi.
Hundreds of women on 10/01 protested in Mombasa against a Senator who publicly criticised President Uhuru Kenyatta. The protesters demanded the Senator apologise.

Five men were admitted to hospital after they were attacked by a gang of armed men in Silaloni, Samburu Sub-County, in Kwale. The camel keepers were attacked by men armed with pangas, bows and arrows as well as other crude weapons on the morning of 02/01. The reason for attack is not known.

Suspected al Shabaab ambushed a police convoy in Lamu on the afternoon of 01/01, injuring security officials and setting a police truck on fire. There was a fierce gun battle at the scene preceded by an explosion. Shortly after the attack police forces in the area launched a large security operation.
A pair of thieves are attacked and nearly lynched before they are rescued.
Vigilantes lynch four suspected cattle thieves in Nyakach on 29/12.

Three people were killed and two others injured after an explosion went off in a vehicle within Mandera town on 28/12. Al Shabaab suspected. The explosion caused a group of locals to hold a demonstration against military forces, mistakenly believing members of the military had been responsible for the deaths of the civilians.

Three people were killed and two others injured after an explosion went off in a vehicle within Mandera town on 28/12. Al Shabaab suspected. The explosion caused a group of locals to hold a demonstration against military forces, mistakenly believing members of the military had been responsible for the deaths of the civilians.

Police clash with a group of matatu operators in the northern suburbs of Mombasa, fifteen injuries reported. The officers were chasing a matatu that had defied orders to stop at the Kenol stage on the Mombasa-Malindi highway near City Mall.
Three are killed in renewed clashes between Kalenjin and Maasais groups in the Olposimoru area of Narok on 27/12.
Two police are attacked on 27/12 along the Lafey-Elwak road, Mandera county. Two others reported dead as well. No immediate claim of responsibility, though al Shabaab are suspected.
Four are injured in continued clashes between Kalenjin and Maasais groups on 26/12 in the Olposimoru area of Narok.
Two suspected thieves are lynched in Ndithini on 26/12.

A member of al Shabaab, attempting to plant a roadside bomb, dies when the device exploded prematurely. The perpetrator was believed to be hurried when he saw that the police had noticed his activities and attempted top stop him. A matter of dispute, the Daily Nation reported police had killed the perpetrator, followed by the explosion.

Many houses are destroyed, causing 2,000 residents to flee following renewed violence between Kalenjins and Maasais groups in the Olposimoru area of Narok on 25/12. Causalities, injuries from the clash are not known.
Four police officers are feared dead following an al Shabaab attack on Bodhei, Lamu County on 25/12.
Two headers are killed in violence between Kalenjin and Maasais in Maasai Mau Narok forest, Narok South Sub-County on 23/12.
One dead and several injured following a border attack between two villages in Kisumu county on 22/12.
Al Shabaab attacks and kills bus two travellers and wounds three others south of Mandera between Kotulo and Daba (Another report indicate the attacks occurred near El Wak) in Mandera County on 21/12.
Al Shabaab attacks and kills three police officers outside Mandera on 21/12. The attack may have been coordinated or related to an attack on bus travellers in the area.
A threat is announced and a bomb later discovered in a Catholic church in Kutu. Its discovery caused congregants to panic and flee. Police later detonated the explosive without injury.
Two are killed during a gun battle between al Shabaab and security forces in Milihoi.
Protestors, drawn from various WTO member countries, staged a protest outside a Nairobi conference over development delays.

A roadside bomb or landmine, suspected to have origin with al Shabaab, detonates in Mandara, targeting and killing a group of five (later determined to be seven) police officers. The landmine was planted inside the customs and border compound. The attack come a day after an ambush on a group of soldiers in the town.
A Senator leads a protest over 'land-grabbing' in a Nairobi area.
Suspected al Shabaab ambush a group of soldiers in (or near) Mandera on 13/12, killing one and wounding two others.
Widows protest in Keringet over government neglect.
An AP police officer opens fire indiscriminately on people in Hulugho on 06/12, injuring one. Authorities are attempting to ascertain if the attack was al Shabaab related.
Al Shabaab attacks Kenyan forces in Lamu on 06/12, seven soldiers killed, ten wounded.
Gachie residents protest against a crime spike in their area on 03/12.

About 200 demonstrators held a peaceful march to the Supreme Court and Parliament buildings (Nairobi - Starehe) where they delivered petitions asking those institutions to do more to tackle corruption in Kenyan government. Police blocked the protesters from entering, fired tear gas canisters and made several arrests.
Residents of Nkunga in Meru blocked a highway in protest of a spate of attack by wild animals in the region. The protesters demanded the Wildlife Service gain better control of the local wildlife.
Garissa residents protest frequent water supply problems on 30/11.
Police engage Moi University students in running battles during a violent protest over the releasing of university student records.
Mombasa traders protest the demolition of their kiosks on 28/11.
Al Shabaab lays siege to on Wajir on 27/11, but are quickly repelled by government soldiers. No reported death or injuries.
Residents of Nayeni, Kilifi county, held a peaceful demo in Malindi town, protesting against the grabbing of 230 acres by the government and private developers.
Al Shabaab overtakes Bula Golol in Garissa Country without resistance, then begins preaching to the residents. Military forces had fled the area prior to the al Shabaab arrival.
Residents of Isibania protest against the delayed construction of a road. Protesters lit a bonfires and urged Governor Okoth Obado to intervene. Business in the town 'came to a halt.'
A soldier was killed and six others injured in the border town of Hulugho after an Al Shabaab IED detonated. Al Shabaab, in taking credit, claims eight dead.
Maasai Mara University students protest poor water services at the university by blocking a road and lighting fires. Six injuries reported.
Hundreds of traders took to the streets on the morning of 19/11 protesting the demolition of kiosks in Ruiru. The protesters lit fires and disrupted traffic along a highway.
Ethiopian-OLF forces and Kenyan police clash in Sololo on 19/11, three police dead. The clash began following an OLF invasion in the area.

A member of al Shabaab escape police, takes the officers weapon and fires several shots. Hundreds of officers cordoned off the area and engaged the suspect in a shootout until he ran out of bullets and was arrested. The suspect was injured.
Al Shabaab kidnaps a teacher at a refugee camp Hagadera. The victim was rescued four days later.
Youths protest leadership corruption at the offices of the EACC on 10/11.

Matatu operators block Langata Road (Nairobi - Langata) in protest of alleged police harassment. Police later contained the situation and towed away three minibuses n parked on the road by the protesting crew. No arrests reported.
Matatu operators block a car park, accusing private operators of driving without licences.

Two communities clashed at the border of Isiolo and Meru counties (roughly near Loloria) on 30/10 following the killing of a Borana boda boda rider. Police said members of the Borana community ganged up to steal motorcycles belonging to their Meru counterparts when they learned one of their own had died. The anger resulting in fighting between the two group, many of whom threw rocks at passing motorists. Police fired tear-gas to disperse the crowds.

Residents of Kiutine in Igembe Central (Meru County) blocked roads leading to Kangeta and Maua towns in protest over conflicts with neighbouring communities. The conflict stemmed from access to local markets.
Jamhuri residents protest the allocation of public land for private development.
Traders in Gatundu Market protested on 26/10, accusing the county government of failing to provide security.
Students of Katheri Boys High School in Imenti Central, riot, destroying their school, in demand their principal be transferred over 'highhandedness.'
One dead, eleven injured and property destroyed in a clash over sand harvesting in Kasikeu.
Locals block the Mpeketoni-Lamu road in protest of pothole problems. The protest disrupted traffic for two hours.
Turkana militia attack a Pokot camp in Narengmor, killing three in revenge of cattle theft.

Pwani University students who attempted to disrupt Mashujaa Day celebrations at Karisa Maitha Grounds were driven back by police. They were demonstrating against the closure of the university due to a water shortage.

The Mombasa Technical University has been closed indefinitely after students went on the rampage to protest increased fees and other management issues they say are hampering learning at the institution.
Boda Boda operators block a road in protest of a colleague who had died as a result of suspected police neglect.

Maseno University students run riot in protest of a fellow student who had fallen and died. Running battles reported with police, teargas and other implements used. Several injuries, one death reported.
A teacher is kidnapped by suspected al Shabaab in Hagadera refugee camp. The teacher was later rescued by Kenyan forces across the border into Somalia.

On 12 October 2015 at 10:30, an INGO vehicle travelling without escort was stopped by a group of five armed men who had fired shots in their direction. The men kidnapped a non-local female Kenyan from the vehicle and fled after coming under fire by police.
Residents of Kabete, Nairobi area hold a protest demonstration over poor roads. Police dispersed the group.
Residents of Kiangombe village in Thika held demonstrations to protest against land grabbing by a private developer.

The Jaramogi Oginga Odinga University of Science and Technology in Bondo has been closed indefinitely after students rioted following controversial elections. The students blocked the Kisumu-Usenge road engaging police in running battles for the better part of 09/10 and 10/10.

The Jaramogi Oginga Odinga University of Science and Technology in Bondo has been closed indefinitely after students rioted following controversial elections. The students blocked the Kisumu-Usenge road engaging police in running battles for the better part of 09/10 and 10/10.
A vigilante group attacked and killed a suspected criminal in Nairobi.

Maseno Universitys administration block was burnt on the night on 07/10 by student arsonists and rioters angry they were barred from campus elections after they failed to meet the election requirements. No injuries reported.
ODM elections in Kisumu county were aborted after violence broke out: a group of rowdy youths attacked a former education minister for unknown reason. 'Scores' injured.
A vigilante mob attacks and nearly killed a suspected cattle thief at Likuyani subcounty, Kakamega.
Students violently protest over delayed loans. Police use tear gas to disperse the group, make ten arrests.
Health workers strike and protest in Kisumu over non-payment of salaries.

Following the killing of a businessman by suspected gangsters, residents of Eldoret violently protest the violence, blocking the Eldoret-Kapsabet highway paralysing transport for hours. Police fired tear gas and rubber bullets against them, who then attempted to storm Langas Police Station in turn.
A group protests in Tetu against the actions of an ODM politician who had derided one they support.
A group protests against genetic food mortification in Nairobi.
Residents lynch a suspected motorcycle thief in the Manyatta section of the city (Nairobi - Kasarani).
National Youth Service employees protest the termination of colleagues in Nairobi.
Teachers protest for pay increase in Muranga.
Residents of Bula Rahma village in the outskirts of Garissa town protest a water shortage in their area.
Striking Bondo subcounty teachers protest at the TSC office(Nairobi - Kamukunji) after a threat to dismiss several of their colleagues.
Teachers in Eldoret protest over pay, cause schools to close.
Striking teachers renew a protest over pay at Uhuru Park (Nairobi - Westlands).
Striking teachers protest over pay in Nairobi. The teachers had been striking for two weeks.

One person injured after being hit by a bullet when garment workers protested poor working conditions at the firm in Mombasa. The workers lit tyres on the road blocking flow of traffic for over two hours before order was restored by police who fired into the air.
A group of youths carrying 'Maendeleo Chap Chap' banners attack people at a WDM rally in Kasikeu. Date unknown - source dated 03/09.

Nyeri residents protest, forcibly entering the officer of the governor and lighting fires in solidarity with striking nurses. The protesters called on the governor to help end the weeks long strike. Police engaged in 'running battles' with the protesters.
Residents of Muranga county blocked MCAs from entering the assembly in Muranga to table an impeachment motion against a preferred politician.
Election violence among the ODM caused two deaths, one in Awendo and the other in Rongo.
Election violence among the ODM caused two deaths, one in Awendo and the other in Rongo.
Farmers in North Rift on 24/08 held a peaceful demonstration on the Iten-Eldoret road, Eldoret to protest over the planned introduction of genetically modified crops.
Boda boda motorcyclists in Limuru town protested after one of them was ordered to pay a bond after the individual is accused of a crime. The protesters lit fires and were later dispersed by police.
Mandera residents held a demonstration to press the government into deploying teachers to the region.
Teachers in Garissa protested over deteriorating education standards in Northeastern.

A young boy is killed during clashes over land between Kapkeny and Kabasirian clans in Kerio Valley. Later reported suggest the battle caused the destructions of many homes and displaced hundreds. Fighting also spilled over into Shaban and Kachesoom areas.
Female APs took to the streets of Kakamega town on 17/08, in a protest against elections from which their representative was allegedly barred.
Two groups of churchgoers clash over the rights to a building.
Turkana attackers kill five in a suspected cattle rustling operation. The attack caused tension in the area.
An al Shabaab-planted explosive attached to a military vehicle causes seven soldier deaths.
'One national INGO staff member got a gunshot wound to the leg and was taken to the hospital to receive medical attention.'

Nine are dead and six are injured in a fight between pastoralists and farmers in Tana River. Additionally, several houses were destroyed. The clashes between Wardei pastoralists and Mijikenda farmers occurred in Wachu Oda in Garsen. A reported 1,500 people displaced as a result of the clashes.
A tussle over the leadership of a church in Vihiga. A house and automobile were destroyed the subsequent unrest.
A members of the National Intelligence Service is killed when a vigilante mob mistook him for a criminal in the Bu_ruburu area (Nairobi - Makadara).
Students of St Pauls Kiwanjani Secondary School protest violently after several students were sent home over disciplinary action. A teacher was reportedly assaulted.
Residents of Athi River protest the police release of a man accused of rape.
Students of Technical University of Kenya embark of a violent protest over 'a stalemate surrounding the validity of the courses.' Police dispersed the protesters following some property damage.
Students from Njoro Boys High School in Nakuru riot over a water supply problem.

More than 600 workers of the China Road and Bridges Company demonstrated on 20/07 against denial of a pay rise to 500 workers. The protest blocked the Nairobi - Mombasa highway at Athi River Steel Plant for an hour. Protesting workers were dispersed by police.
Reports indicate that Al Shabaab overtook Milimani village in Lamu on the night of 18/07. No violence was reported.
Students of Gatamaiyu Boys High School riot, destroy school property. Authorities were not clear as to the reason of the protest.

Around 15 July 2015 (month of), police officers in Nairobi (Starehe, Nairobi) beat up a gay man and his three roommates to extract confessions that they were gay. The police was called by one of the men after a mob threatened to burst into his apartment.
Around 15 July 2015 (month of), a group of people in Nairobi (Starehe, Nairobi) held an Ugandan refugee and three of his roommates, beating them while trying to extract confessions they were gay.
Students in Likoni violently protest over delayed syllabus completion ahead of an exam.
Groups students of Moi University clash violently over forthcoming student elections, destroying property. Police engaged the rioters and made several arrests.
Al Shabaab targets police with an IED in Lamu on 13/07. Three deaths reported.
Students from Nguviu Boys High School in Embu North shattered window panes of their buildings for allegedly being refused to eat directly from sufurias.
Al Shabaab attacks a police convoy, including a civilian bus travelling in Mkunumbi, no reported causalities.

Al Shabaab attacks Mandera town, throwing grenades into homes while people slept on 07/07. 14 dead. Al Shabaab later officially claimed responsibility, declaring they were specifically targeting Christians.

Armed men attacked a passenger bus on 07/07 at Mpekatoni border town. There were no immediate reports of any casualties. Police later report the attack was not carried out by al Shabaab, but rather an unidentified group of locals.
A group protests against homosexuality in Nairobi.
A suspected murderer is lynched in Ganze.
A senior, off-duty National Intelligence Service officer is shot and killed on 03/07 by two unidentified assailants in Mombasa.
Nine are killed and six others injured on 01/07 following an attack by members of the Marhani clan of Somalia on Arabia.
Hundreds of boda boda operators hold a demonstration outside City Hall in Nairobi (Nairobi - Starehe) accusing city askaris of harassment.

Residents of Isiolo town in Eastern Province held a demo on 30/06 over the disappearance and abduction of several men. Hundreds of women held a peaceful rally demanding answers from the government. Many of the protesters accused the Kenya Wildlife Services for the disappearance of the men.

Youths from Chuka Igambangombe Constituency demonstrated in Chuka Town during recruitment by the National Youth Service, criticizing the criteria used to fill the 1,440 vacancies. The protest lasted the majority of the afternoon.
Parents of Muslim students in Kwale protest after it is alleged their children were forced to attend church services while attending school.
Staff of a garment company in Athi River protest after the suspension of their chief shop steward.
One person was killed and two others injured in an attack by suspected Al-Shabaab gunmen in Mandera Town on the night of 26/06. All of the victims are 'non-locals,' origin not known.

Youths attached to the National Youth Service slum-upgrading project in Kisumu on 23/06 staged a demo in Nairobi centre (Nairobi - Starehe) to protest against calls by Cord leaders that the project be investigated on financial corruption grounds.
Residents from Obunga slums in Kisumu on 22/06 held demonstrations in support of a politician they believed is being unfairly criticised.
Three KDF members are injured in an al Shabaab IED attack Milimani on 21/06.

Youth demonstrators protesting against National Youth Service slum projects as well as against Devolution Cabinet Secretary Ann Waiguru. The youth started demonstrating at 7pm at Kiberas Olympic stage, where they lit bonfires and barricaded the road. The group believed the NYS and Waiguru are corrupt. The protests may have continued the following day, as there was a reported heavy police presence.
Suspected al Shabaab shot and killed a chief of Erib location in Wajir on 20/06.
Two university students are lynched by a vigilante group over suspected theft 'at the weekend.'
Hospital staff protest staff leadership in the suburban Nairobi area of Moi (Nairobi - Starehe) on 19/06.

20 people are killed in Durogo [phonetic] in Mandera County in what has been described as revenge attacks by Garre [clan] fighters following the killings of their clansmen. Perpetrators are not known. Date unclear - source dated 17/06.

Police in Siaya were forced to shoot in the air several times when a group of 'rowdy' youths disrupted a meeting chaired by Governor Cornel Rasanga in Yala. Chanting anti-Rasanga slogans, the group claimed the governor had no place in Yala, which is in Gem constituency. No causalities reported.

Five pastoralists are killed by unidentified gunmen at Wari walo village some 10 kilometres from Kenya border. Those killed were three children (two boys and a girl), their father and a close relative. The five had recently left Elmole in pursuit of pasture and water for their animals.
Residents of Salgaa Township, Nakuru blocked Nakuru-Eldoret highway accusing the Governor of denying them development. Several vehicles were reportedly burnt during the protest.

Al Shabaab attacks several locations of Lamu Island and were able to briefly overtake the area known as 'Mangai,' an area they found with little resistance. Other places attacked included a school and a military camp. Military forces eventually repelled the attackers. 'Several' casualties reported, eleven of which were recorded as al Shabaab. Later reports suggest a British-born member of al Shabaab (known as Thomas Evans or Abdul Akim) may have been a leader in the attack and is among the dead. Another suspect of the attack was apprehended on 20/06.
Marsabit non-local residents protest over insecurity following a recent spate of killings in which they were targeted.
Residents of Baraka Estate (Nairobi - Embakasi South) protest over poor roads in their area.

Non-violent activity: Al Shabaab reportedly erects a series of road blocks between Garba Tula and Modogashe townships [north-eastern Kenya] for purposes of extorting money from motorists. Despite these assertions, the local government denies these claims. Exact date unknown.

Hundreds of residents of Dadaab took to the streets on 06/08 to protest over the alleged sacking of 13 local employees by the World Food Programme (WFP). Waving placards, demonstrators marched through the town before heading to the main UNHCR headquarters offices gate where they camped for several hours.
Youth employed to repair roads at Jomvu in Mikindani, Mombasa county held a protest march on 08/06 over delayed pay.

At least 10 pastoralists from Isiolo have been killed in clashes with Laikipia residents after the herders invade the area with hundreds of animals. The herders also shot two security personnel after they were ordered to vacate the land during the clashes.
At least three people were killed and several others injured on the morning of 06/06 in inter-community clashes at Lowangila in Isiolo County. The clash may be related to rights to cattle or land.

Suspected al Shabaab opened fire at a residential area of Wajir on 06/06, killing three persons. Officials and residents said the attackers were believed to have been seeking to kill a local administrator who lives close to the scene of the attack and is known to be on an al Shabaab 'wanted' list for speaking out against the sects activities in the region.

Two non-local residents of Marsabit are killed in mysterious circumstances by unidentified assailants. Non-locals claim that they are being targeted in assassinations by police. The police deny the allegations.
Al Shabaab creates a heavy presence in Lafey village effectively 'taking over' the village. The presence of al Shabaab caused several villagers to flee for safety.

Residents protested for a second day against the closure of a public corridor leading to Lake Naivasha. The more than 400 residents blocked the road using boulders and light fires to protest the closure demanded justice. Police entered the area and engaged the demonstrators in running battles. Spats of violence continued into the second day. 'Scores' injured.

Transport on Moi South Lake road in Naivasha was paralysed for more than three hours as residents protested the closure of a public corridor leading to Lake Naivasha. The more than 400 residents blocked the road using boulders and light fires to protest the closure demanded justice. Police entered the area and engaged the demonstrators in running battles. Spats of violence continued into the second day. 'Scores' injured.
Al Shabaab attacks a police post Yumbis on the night of 25/05, killing 20. Al Shabaab had also attacked the area the previous week.
Al Shabaab gunmen attack Yumbis and Wel Marer villages in Fafi, each about 80 Km north east of Garissa. Security forces pushed back the attackers, no reported causalities.
Al Shabaab gunmen attack Yumbis and Wel Marer villages in Fafi, each about 80 Km north east of Garissa. Security forces pushed back the attackers, no reported causalities.
Residents of Kiangage in Muranga on the night of 19/05 set ablaze a matatu driver that killed a boda boda rider in a recent accident.
Residents of Muoroto Kamiti village in Kiambu Town constituency protest against the grabbing of 2,400 acres by a private developer.
Al Shabaab 'catches two military posts (in Sangailu and Hulugho) by surprise,' no violence reported.
Al Shabaab 'catches two military posts (in Sangailu and Hulugho) by surprise,' no violence reported.
Ethiopian soldiers armed with AK-47 rifles cross into Kenya aboard 10 vehicles and reportedly take over a police station in North Horr.

Following the disappearance of three people residents of Kinna protest, accusing the Kenya Wildlife Service of kidnapping. The residents marched to the Meru National Park and allegedly set a fire at the park. One is killed and eleven injured after the police engaged the protesters.
Residents protest the removal of a roadblock by police believing the action to be 'suspect.'
Police clash with students protesting the death of colleague, seven injuries reported.
Two suspected Al-Shabab gunmen and a police officer killed in shoot out at Dadaab Hamey Patrol Base in Garissa.
Women in Makueni county held a peaceful demonstration to oppose a bill on the implementation of the two-thirds gender rule. The protest took place in Wote town.
Nurses at Meru teaching hospital protest over non-payment of salaries.
Tenants continue protests for a second day following a forced eviction and resident shooting. No violence reported.
A resident is shot and killed when a group resisted a forced eviction. Following the shooting tenants lit fires and sang anti-oppression themed songs.

Turkana raiders attack a Pokot village close to Nadome along the Turkana-East Pokot district border, killing 18 residents. Following the attack a Pokot militia assembled, chasing the attackers to nearby Kogh-Tuw village and killing 36.
Residents protest against Baringo county insecurity in Marigat.

Turkana raiders attack a Pokot village close to Nadome along the Turkana-East Pokot district border, killing 18 residents. Following the attack a Pokot militia assembled, chasing the attackers to nearby Kogh-Tuw village and killing 36.

At least fifteen people are feared dead in fresh attack among rival villages or groups in Baragoi, Samburu County. Eight people were reportedly killed during a raid at Lomirok early Sunday morning (03/05). Unconfirmed reports indicate that another six, among them women and children, were killed at Sarma along the Samburu-Marsabit border that evening.
April 30, 2015, unidentified assailants repeatedly hit the editor of the Eldoret-based Mirror Weekly, with blunt objects and killed him.
Hundreds of traders from Nairobis Woodley-Jamhuri market protested alleged grabbing of their market by a private developer.
Workers protest poor working conditions and pay in Jomvu.
Residents of Ndagani, in Igambangombe constituency on the morning of 27/04 blocked the Meru- Nairobi highway to protest against the poor sate of Ndagani-Gicusa road.
The more than 100 traders held a demonstration in Gakindu town over a closed slaughterhouse that they claim cannot be reopened due to bureaucratic oversight.
Suspected Somali Al-Shabaab kidnapped two Kenyan teachers on the evening of 24/04 in the Mandera border town.
10,000 members of the National Hospital Insurance Fund in Nyandarua county protest against a rate increase in Ndunyu Nderu.

Heavily armed gunmen suspected to be members of Al-Shabaab on the morning of 23/04 kidnapped senior Arabia chief in Mandera County along the Mandera-Arabia road. The chief was driven across the border into Somalia where he was killed at Gadoon Dhowe, Beled Xawo District.
Boda Boda operators protest alleged police harassment by barricading the Narok-Bomet road.

Boda Boda operators block a road and light fires in protest against a police 'crackdown' against them. They said police ask for bribes and frequently arrest them for no genuine reason. A similar protest was held the following day in a nearby area.

actor1: Police Forces of Kenya (2013-2022) General Service Unit
notes: On 17 April 2015, officers from Kenya's anti-riot police, the General Service Unit (GSU), beat and kicked Nation journalist Nehemiah Okwembah and Citizen television cameraman Rueben Ogachi at Bombi village on the outskirts of the government-owned Kulalu Galana Ranch in Tana River county
Hospital workers protest unpaid dues.
Non-violent activity: Ten armed members of al Shabaab hijack a bus carrying ten passengers, deboard them and take the bus across the border into Somalia. No violence reported.
Traders protest county taxes in Thika.
A suspected rustler was killed by a mob in Central Kanyamkago ward, Uriri subcounty in Migori county. One of his accomplices was injured while the rest escaped.
Pokot militia kill a goat herder in Chemoe.
A mob lynched two suspected cattle thieves in Likuyani subcounty, Kakamega.
Defusal: Police uncover and remove an IED in Mandera County, near the Somali border on 12/04.
Kenyan police on 11/04 shot dead two al Shabaab suspects in an incident that left one police officer injured in Kwale.
Protesters of police practices stone a journalist covering the event. The journalist suffered a head and knee injury.
Traders in Kisii protest a tax increase.

The bodies of two men are discovered in Kamirithu village on the morning of 08/04. Their deaths may have occurred the evening before. The motive of the attack as well as their identifies of the victims are not known.
Traders in Limuru protest increased fees. Date(s) not known - the protest was described as 'ongoing.'
Factory workers protest a dispute with management.
Students protest the Garissa attack in Nairobi, calling on the government to do more for security.
Hundreds of Somalis took to the streets in the Nairobis Somali-dominated Eastleigh neighbourhood on Sunday [5 April] to protest against the recent deadly attack on Garissa university.
Garissa residents protest a recent al Shabaab attack on a school in their town. Date unknown - source dated 04/04.
Hundreds of Kenyan residents have rallied at a state sponsored protest in the capital Nairobi to condemn recent Al-Shabaab attack on Gaarisa University premises.

Al Shabaab gunmen attack Garissa University during the morning hours in an operation that lasted the majority of the day. Almost all of the 148 people killed were students and another 79 people were injured.

Al Shabaab gunmen attack Garissa University during the morning hours in an operation that lasted the majority of the day. Four attackers were killed during the siege, and the police are holding another five individuals for questioning.

At least one person was killed and three others injured on the morning of 01/04 when masked gunmen attacked a non-governmental organisations compound at the Dadaab Refugee Camp. The attack occurred during the early morning hours, perpetrators not known.
Two groups of demonstrators in Kilifi clashed outside the Kilifi police station as they differed over whether Governor Amason Kingi should step aside over corruption allegations.
Hundreds of travellers heading to either Tanzania or Kenya are stranded at Namanga border after Kajiado residents blocked the road to protest over a missing taxi driver.
Three suspected carjackers are lynched by a mob in Kariene, Meru County.
Baringo county residents protest reoccurring attack by Pokot bandits. The protesters marched throughout the county, eventually ending in Kabarnet.

A group of Kenyan youths protest a Chinese Restaurants policy of refusing entry to local people during the nigh time hours. The protest turned violent, however, when the group began looting the restaurant. No injury reported.
A vigilante mob 'last week' lynched a criminal suspect. Source dated 31/03.
Traders blocked the Eldoret-Nakuru highway at Burnt Forest, protesting against increased licence fees and poor services.
A senior Mombasa police detective is gunned down in an apparent well organized assassination. The perpetrator is not unknown, though the source cites al Shabaab presence in the area.
Fruit factory workers protest poor working conditions in Bibirioni, Limuru. Date not clear - source dated 24/03.
A groups of youths protest the Mandera Deputy Governor during a rally in Mandara.
Parents of two schools in Nakuru hold a demonstration to protest the grabbing of a section of the school land by a private developer.
Students of Rongo University College state a protest after a residential hall is burned. The protest and fire may be related to a recent election which caused tension in the area.
A suspected murderer is lynched by a vigilante group in Mukuro.

Residents violently protest the release of two murder suspects on bond. The protesters blocked the nearby Eldoret-Chavakali road for hours and injured one police officer. Additionally, several shops and houses were burned.
On 23 March 2015, a woman was killed, allegedly by police, during a demonstration in Malindi to protest against the tax increase by the Kilifi county government. Police deny they used live rounds.

A Standard newspaper journalist in Eldoret town said he was kidnapped outside his house on March 22, 2015 by people who questioned him about stories he had been writing about irregular land acquisitions by individuals in positions of influence. The journalist said he was threatened, drugged, and discovered unconscious two days later more than 40 kilometers away.

A riotous mob attacked a man, killed him and burnt down his house (in Itumbu) after suspecting him of being in a criminal gang. The attack came after villagers carried out a violent protest against insecurity in the region. A protester was injured after the suspects son tried to stop them from burning their house. A similarly motivated protest occurred the previous day. The protesters burnt three houses belonging to a family suspected of harbouring a criminal gang.
Residents of Mandera County demonstrate against recent area violence by al Shabaab. Date not known: source dated 21/03.

A riotous mob attacked a man, killed him and burnt down his house (in Itumbu) after suspecting him of being in a criminal gang. The attack came after villagers carried out a violent protest against insecurity in the region. A protester was injured after the suspects son tried to stop them from burning their house. A similarly motivated protest occurred the previous day. The protesters burnt three houses belonging to a family suspected of harbouring a criminal gang.
Hundreds of Mandera County residents took to the streets of the border town on 20/03 protesting over recent insecurity in the area. The protesters called for the removal of the county commissioner.

A riotous mob attacked a man, killed him and burnt down his house (in Itumbu) after suspecting him of being in a criminal gang. The attack came after villagers carried out a violent protest against insecurity in the region. A protester was injured after the suspects son tried to stop them from burning their house. A similarly motivated protest occurred the previous day. The protesters burnt three houses belonging to a family suspected of harbouring a criminal gang.
An IED explodes in Mandera following a similar attack across the Somali border in Beled Hawo. No reported causalities.
Four are killed and their bodies burnt in a grenade attack on a Wajir shop. Perpetrators not known.
Al Shabaab carries out the second attack in two days in Mandera. One death, three injuries reported. In the following days the death total was raised from 1 to 4.
Employees of Kenya Methodist University protest a reduction of their allowances by the institution (Nairobi - Starehe).

Three people were killed and eight more wounded when al Shabaab launched a cross-border raid on a convoy carrying Mandera county governor Ali Roba. The governor escaped unharmed. The convoy was travelling either to or from Nairobi.
Al Shabaab attack, and then later claim responsibility for the death of four in Wajir. Three other injured.

West Pokot county residents held a demonstration to protest against increase in road accidents on the Kitale-Lodwar road. The residents barricaded the road for the better part of the day, halting transport. They felled big trees on the road, blocking it completely at Kamatira market. Kamatira Primary School pupils also joined the demonstration, saying many of their colleagues have died on the road.
Traders protest an eviction notice along the Malaba-Eldoret road.

Three pirates have been shot dead in Migingo Island by Ugandan security forces. The pirates, believed to be Tanzanian nationals, were accosted inside the lake while robbing fishermen. Three other pirates were arrested. Kenya and Uganda have both staked claim to the fish-rich island - a row that has lasted since 2002.
Two unidentified sub tribes clash over land at Kathanje (Kathangei), Chuka Igambangombe constituency. One death, plus other injuries reported.
More than 200 Kisii county government employees demonstrated at Governor James Ongwaes office protesting they have not been paid for nine months.
Residents of Mukurwe-ini marched to the sub-county hospitals mortuary and took away the body of a man who was allegedly shot by a police officer in protest of the killing.
Students of Kilgoris Boys National School pelt their principals home with stones following learning of poor exam results.
Residents of Tseikuru protest, demand the removal of the local district commissioner. Police dispersed the group.
Teachers of a Mandera school are attacked and injured when students from a neighbouring school targeted them in blame for the cancellation of recent exams.
Following an road accident involving students, students of Thiru Secondary School barricade a road in protest.

Students of ST Mathias Busia Boys Secondary School strike over test grades, vandalise school property, broke into teachers residential houses, staff rooms, offices, and stores, the canteen and laboratories. No reported injury.
A vigilante group attack and sets alight four robbery suspects at different nearby locations: Three in Kathiani and one in Kituvu.
A vigilante group attack and sets alight four robbery suspects at different nearby locations: Three in Kathiani and one in Kituvu.

Television viewers protest analogue signal switch off at outside Communications Authority offices on Waiyaki Way, Nairobi (Nairobi - Westlands). The switch off forces viewers to purchase a digital apparatus.
Boda boda drivers protest a tax increase over two consecutive days in Mumias.

One person was killed and two others injured in an attack by suspected Al-Shabaab gunmen in Mandera Town on the night of 25/02. The victims were witnessed crossing from nearby Somalia at an earlier date and are suspected to be Somalis
Tugan and Pokot militias exchange fire over grazing land and cattle ownership at Kapndasum in Marigat. An unarmed bystander was killed in the shootout, several others missing.

More than 200 businesspeople in Kisii town staged a demonstration to protest against grabbing of land where they operate. The traders protested against a decision by the county government to move them from outside the Kisii Municipal Market.
Three quarters of students at Leshau Boys High School boycotted classes, protesting alleged poor hygiene in the institution. The students marched peacefully to the Nyahururu-Nyeri highway.
Boda boda drivers protest a tax increase over two consecutive days in Mumias.
Farmers protest in Kinangop for a second day, engage in running battles with police. One dead, several others injured.

University of Nairobi students protested the death of their colleague who succumbed to injuries following an pedestrian-auto accident last week. The students pelted vehicles passing through Waiyaki Way and University Way (Nairobi - Westlands) with stones, causing a traffic problems.
Street traders hold a 'mostly peaceful' demonstration in Kutui over a tax levied against them. No report of violence.

Farmers blocked the Nairobi-Naivasha highway in Kinangop for more than four hours protesting a wind project which they allege would displace several families. During the protest, a house and a vehicle were burnt down as the farmers engaged police in running battles. There were unconfirmed reports that two women and a boy were rushed to a private hospital with bullet wounds.
Residents of Ukasi, Mwingi Central, hold a peaceful demonstration to protest against prolonged water shortage.
Students protest violently for a second day against sexual misconduct alleged against a school leader.
Hundreds of Voi residents took to the streets on 19/02 in a protest for the arrest of a Marungu ward rep over alleged sexual abuse.
A boda boda operator was killed by colleagues and his body set on fire (18/02) on the Webuye-Malaba road at Chekulo, Bungoma. The victim was suspected of murder.

Groups of students clashed along ethnic lines with 'members of the community' over the removal of the universities vice chancellor over alleged sexual misconduct and murder. The identities of the ethnic groups are not known. No reported injuries or causalities in the second melee.

A Senator and ten others are assaulted by riot police when they staged a protest at the University of Eldoret in an effort to force the removal of the vice chancellor Teresa Akenga, whom area leaders accused of nepotism and skewed employment. The protest was reported as peaceful.
On 18 February 2015, police in Kwale (Matuga, Kwale) arrested two men and threatened them with violence to extract confessions that they were gay. Doctors conducted forced anal examinations.
Residents of Umande, Laikipia East sub county, held a demonstration against the abstraction of Sirimon River by a privately held dam.
A mob stones a suspected murderer to death.
Around 15 February 2015 (month of), residents in Watamu in Kilifi (Kilifi North, Kilifi) attacked a funeral attended by a number of LGBT people.

On 14 February 2015, Embu Governor Martin Wamboras supporters (TNA) and those of Runyenjes MP Cecily Mbarire (Party of National Unity) clashed in Embu town (Manyatta, Embu). Wamboras supporters were demonstrating against the High Courts decision to remove Wambora from office when those supporters of Mbarire attacked the group. The two groups engaged in running battles before riot police intervened. Injuries not reported.
Unknown assailants on the evening of 13/02 hurled two hand grenades at police officers on patrol in Wajir town. No reported injuries.
Police in Thika shot in the air to disperse a crowd who had planned on attacking an officer who they believed had earlier assaulted a woman.

Traders of Burma Market, Nairobi used flaming tyres to block Jogoo Road (Nairobi - Makadara) in a demo against alleged land grabbing on [the morning of 13/02]. The traders hurled stones at motorists preventing access to the road and causing a traffic snarl up. [The rioters] engaged police in running battles as tear gas canisters were lobbed to disperse them.
Residents of Kabete constituency held a demonstration at Wangige trading centre over the pace of investigations into area MP George Muchais murder, which occurred on 07/02.

Traders in Molo town held a demonstration to protest against the poor state of the Molo-Kibunjia road. The traders barricaded the road with stones and flaming tyres, saying the government is deliberately ignoring them.

A prominent Kenyan MP of the Jubilee Coalition (George Muchai) was shot dead along with two bodyguards and a driver in the centre of Nairobi in the early hours of 07/02. The masked perpetrators, who were driving an automobile with Ugandan licence plates, escaped. A senior police officer said the killing looked like an execution-style hit.

A group of cattle herdsmen blocked the Mai Mahiu-Narok road (B3) for several hours after several of the herd were killed when they were hit with a lorry. The herdsmen demanded compensation for their loss by the colliding driver. They barred police officers from removing the truck or the carcasses until the matter was resolved.

Traders pelted Nairobi Governor Evans Kidero with mud during an appearance. The traders stalls were burned the previous evening for which the traders blamed the local government. The governors bodyguards shot into the air to disperse the mob.

Three people were critically injured after a hand grenade was hurled at a food kiosk in Mandera town. The reason for the attack is not known. The perpetrators escaped. Authorities suspect one of the victims may have been linked to al Shabaab.

Police have fired in the air and lobbed teargas to disperse hundreds of City Park Market traders who are protesting the burning down of their stalls, which they claim was sabotage. The traders blocked Limuru Road to traffic (Nairobi - Westlands), demanding compensation from the government after the fire destroyed their goods and other properties. The rioters threw stones at passing motorists and police.

Police fired teargas at students of Kenya Medical Training College (Nairobi - Langata)who were protesting over the death of their classmate. The student had committed suicide after being removed from an exam over unpaid fees.

Four killed and several injured during a Pokot raid on a Turkana village. Authorities claimed the attacks were meant to scare members of the Turkana community into leaving Lomelo, Silale and Nadome villages, which Pokots have laid claim.
A suspect in the murder of a boda boda operator in Sindo, Suba subcounty, was snatched from the police by residents and beaten to death in Sindo.

Around 3 February 2015 (week of), a group of residents in Diani (Msambweni, Kwale) beat up a man accused of being gay. They slashed a bottle on his neck and collarbone. The man lost consciousness and went to the hospital for three days.
800 Mandera teachers protest al Shabaab spurred insecurity in their region at the KNUT headquarters in Nairobi (Nairobi - Starehe). After several hours the group marched to the parliament building.

Nairobi Aviation College students blocked Kimathi Street (Nairobi - Starehe) to protest an unflattering expose on sale of certificates aired on television. The students, who carried twigs and college banners, threw stones at Nation Centre breaking doors and windows and chased journalists who were taking pictures. Police dispersed the students twice, the second time after they had regrouped. Tear gas used. 12 arrests reported.
Students in Wajir protest a teacher shortage in the area.

Protesters continue their demonstration against the detention of a group of lawmakers. Protestors blocked traffic on the Nairobi-Narok highway, police responded with teargas and live fire, clashes followed. No reported deaths.

Protestors in Narok county on Wednesday night blocked roads in the area after Senator Stephen Ole Ntutu and four legislators were earlier arrested over demonstrations that occurred on Monday. The protestors who were armed with sticks and arrows blocked the road in Ololunga area and another in Katagala for more than two hours over the arrests, demanding their release. Police had to fire tear gas at the protestors to disperse them.

Protestors in Narok county on Wednesday night blocked roads in the area after Senator Stephen Ole Ntutu and four legislators were earlier arrested over demonstrations that occurred on Monday. The protestors who were armed with sticks and arrows blocked the road in Ololunga area and another in Katagala for more than two hours over the arrests, demanding their release. Police had to fire tear gas at the protestors to disperse them.
Transporters blocked the highway near Mlolongo on 26/01 to protest the closing of access roads by police, who they charged with corruption.
Protesting the availability of jobs offered by a power company, residents block the a road leading to work site in Kargi for several days, holding hostage a truck driver ferrying supplies.
A group of Boba Boda operators lynch a 16-year old girl of suspected theft.

At least two people were feared dead and dozens others wounded in Narok when protests to oust Governor Samuel Tunai turned chaotic. The protesters accused the governor of corruption. Among those wounded was area police chief Paul Letting and two of his juniors, police said of the protests, which brought Narok town to a standstill for several hours. At least one of the dead was shot by police. Several arrests were recorded in the following days, including five Senators.
Students of Limuko Secondary School in Bahati protest, demanding the transfer of their principal alleging 'highhandedness.'
Protesting the availability of jobs offered by a power company, residents block the a road leading to work site in Kargi for several days, holding hostage a truck driver ferrying supplies.
Three men are killed when Kikuyu and Maasai groups clashed over a farms ownership.
Protesting the availability of jobs offered by a power company, residents block the a road leading to work site in Kargi for several days, holding hostage a truck driver ferrying supplies.
Protesting the availability of jobs offered by a power company, residents block the a road leading to work site in Kargi for several days, holding hostage a truck driver ferrying supplies.
Boda boda operators in Amagoro town protest alleged police harassment.
Three unidentified gunmen shoot and kill an Imam at a construction site in Likoni. Investigators have not established a motive.

Students and activists protesting against a school land dispute clash with police Langata. Rocks thrown, tear gas implemented. Five pupils, two journalists and a police officer were injured and two activists arrested during the incident. The event became a scandal in the following days after it was learned that several of the injured students were young children.
Two groups of protesters clash - those for and against a withdrawal of Sh60 million annual sponsorship for four schools in Mtwapa. Injuries not known.
A group of women protesting in support of circumcision of girls lured activists opposed to the practice and attacked them at Enoosaen Village in Transmara, Narok County. Injuries not known.
Githurai residents on 15/01 morning lynched four people who they accused of engaging in criminal activities in the area.

On 14 January 2015, residents of Machakos hurled stones at county Askaris (County Enforcement Officers), to stop them from towing away the deputy governors car. A woman broke her leg when she was allegedly beaten by the Askaris.
Suburban Nairobi residents set a suspected thief alight.

A group of Nairobi-based journalists were ejected from a reception area at the United Nations complex (Nairobi - Westlands) in Kenyas capital after launching a protest over Al-Jazeera journalists jailed in Egypt.

Pokot cattle rustlers struck Namawanga village inhabited by members of the Luhya community and shot dead a local farmer before stealing three bulls from his home. In revenge, Luhya tribesmen hacked to death a Pokot man after they found him ferrying two passengers to Karnyarkwat market. The killing of the man sparked off protest from members of the Pokot community who thronged to Kapkoi market vowing to revenge over the killing of their tribesmen.
URP supporters disrupt a demonstration in Bomet concerning the location of a university, no reported violence. Police forces dispersed the two groups.

Pokot cattle rustlers struck Namawanga village inhabited by members of the Luhya community and shot dead a local farmer before stealing three bulls from his home. In revenge, Luhya tribesmen hacked to death a Pokot man who operates a motor cycle taxis after they found him ferrying two passengers to Karnyarkwat market. The killing of the man sparked off protest from members of the Pokot community who thronged to Kapkoi market vowing to revenge over the killing of their tribesmen.

Pokot cattle rustlers struck Namawanga village inhabited by members of the Luhya community and shot dead a local farmer before stealing three bulls from his home. In revenge, Luhya tribesmen hacked to death a Pokot man who operates a motor cycle taxis after they found him ferrying two passengers to Karnyarkwat market. The killing of the man sparked off protest from members of the Pokot community who thronged to Kapkoi market vowing to revenge over the killing of their tribesmen.

An unidentified attacker targeted a crowded Mombasa church, but are repulsed by police guarding the door. Police engaged the assailant in a shootout before he escaped. The reason for the attack is not known. One church official was reported dead following the incident.
Two demonstrators were shot and injured by police in Mau Narok during a protest against increased road accidents.
Traders at Kalundu market held a demonstration in Kitui town, protesting against high market charges by the county government.
Fishermen clash with police after officials closed a corridor leading to Lake Naivasha and Karagita beach in Naivasha. No reported injuries.
Following an attack by armed robbers in Ol Moran village of Laikipia residents protest insecurity.
More than 1,000 teachers from Buuri, North Imenti, South Imenti and Meru Central sub counties protest in Meru. The teachers were on strike, calling for better salaries.
Medical worker protesters clash with a group that was attempting to stop them. One man is injured after he was hit in the face with a stone.
Hundreds of Athi River sub county workers protested over a irregular payment from Machakos county government.
Pokot gunmen killed a school guard during the late morning hours. Motive unknown.
Teachers strike, protest over poor working conditions.

Youths took to Ngong Road in Nairobi (Nairobi - Westlands) and adjacent streets to protest the death of former Prime Minister Raila Odingas son, who died in unclear circumstances. The protesters demanded to know the cause of death. The demo lasted several hours.
Boda boda riders and traders protest a new law that prohibits animals to travel through the CBD of Bomet.
